【第1頁】
Together towards 
a successful future
Information for international students


【第2頁】
© Foto: Bernd Ottow

【第3頁】
Aschaffenburg University of Applied Sciences 
(Aschaffenburg UAS) is one of Germany’s leading 
young universities. Since becoming a teaching 
institution in 1995, Aschaffenburg UAS has 
offered forward-looking programmes geared 
towards putting the latest research into practice. 
Today, more than 180 professors and lecturers 
teach approximately 3,750 students. 
Top-ranked programmes
Due to its achievements in teaching and research 
as well as the international outlook of its 
programmes of study, Aschaffenburg UAS has 
been rated among Germany’s leading institutions 
in various rankings.
Meaningful interdisciplinary collaboration
Due to its focused yet interconnected three-
faculty organisational structure, students have 
easy access to opportunities for interdisciplinary 
collaboration. Business and law students have 
a chance to gain technology expertise, for 
instance, while engineers can brush up on their 
management skills. 
Why Aschaffenburg University  
of Applied Sciences?
© Foto: Bernd Ottow
3

【第4頁】
Informal and welcoming atmosphere
The compact campus is easily walkable, and the 
small size creates a strong community feeling. 
On a typical day on campus, you might bump 
into friends on your way to class, eat lunch with a 
professor in the dining hall, and carry out research 
with classmates in a high-tech laboratory – all 
within a five- or ten-minute walk. 
Excellence in teaching and personal support
World-class teaching is one of Aschaffenburg 
UAS’s most important goals, and its teachers 
have extensive resources to ensure that you 
maximise your learning. Small class sizes mean 
that your professors and lecturers are available to 
you for extra guidance or support, both during and 
outside of seminars. 
Modern infrastructure, high-tech facilities
Classrooms, lecture halls, offices, and laboratories 
are housed in historical buildings that have 
been completely renovated in order to provide a 
modern, high-tech study environment. Laboratory 
and workshop facilities are cutting-edge, offering 
you access to the latest equipment in your chosen 
field, and classrooms and study spaces are 
equipped with modern computing technology. 
Friendly town in a booming business region
Aschaffenburg lies in the heart of the Frankfurt-
Rhine-Main business region – Germany’s 
industrial and business core. We cultivate 
extensive partnerships with regional and global 
companies, offering students ample opportunities 
to put theory into practice, find part-time jobs, 
internships, and post-graduation employment. 
At the same time, Aschaffenburg is small and 
friendly, with lovely architecture and historical 
charm. Extensive public transportation provides 
easy access to the rest of the region and 
Germany, giving students the best of both worlds.
© Foto: stock.adobe.de – Sina Ettmer4

【第5頁】
“My semester at Aschaffenburg UAS was for 
sure the best time in my whole student life. 
Living on the campus was such a convenient 
and amazing experience not only because 
of having a university close to where I lived 
but also because of being part of a place 
where all of the students are concentrated 
in one place and the possibility to meet 
new people easily was fantastic! Despite 
an amazing social life, the university is very 
helpful and extremely organized which helps 
in the adaptation process. The atmosphere 
there is cozy and I felt very warmly welcomed 
and treated for the whole time. This place 
is my second home, my place on earth and 
although I left, I am sure that I will be  
coming back very often."
Melania from Poland
© Foto: Bernd Ottow 5

【第6頁】
„I choose to come to the Aschaffenburg, because 
I read about its high quality of education. The 
lecturers at a university of applied sciences in 
Germany are required to have several years of 
experience, which is not common in Hungary. 
Speaking from my experience, this university 
fulfilled my expectations and even outperformed 
them. Both the education level and the social life 
was better than I could ever imagine. I learned a 
lot here and broadened my views about higher 
education, not to mention that I was lucky enough 
to participate in several exceptional trips with 
Business Seminar Germany and Introduction 
to the EU courses. Concerning my social 
life, these two semesters were truly the 
best days of my life. I have collected a 
lot of new friends and unforgettable 
memories in Aschaffenburg, so if you 
are hesitating, I can just say GO FOR IT!“ 
Tamara from Hungary
© Foto: Bernd Ottow6

【第7頁】
Academic information and application
In general, German higher education institutions 
are classified as either universities or universities 
of applied sciences. As a university of applied 
sciences, Aschaffenburg UAS focuses more on 
gaining skills and knowledge which can be directly 
applied in professional life. Universities of applied 
sciences are more industry-oriented than their 
counterparts and professors must have practical 
work experience outside of the higher education 
sector. Both types of institutions can issue 
bachelor’s and master’s degrees.
Course offer
The English-taught courses cover a wide 
range of subjects. Depending on your German 
language proficiency, you may also choose from 
a wide variety of courses taught in German. At 
Aschaffenburg UAS you can study business 
administration, real estate management, 
computing, renewable energies, mechatronics, 
sales, and material sciences, to name a few.
 www.th-ab.de/course-offer
7

【第8頁】
German as a Foreign Language
Learning German can be very useful to connect 
with the locals. Aschaffenburg UAS offers German 
language courses for all skill levels – whether 
you are starting out as a beginner or at a more 
advanced level. In addition to the courses offered 
during the semester, Aschaffenburg UAS offers 
four-week intensive German courses in August.
 www.th-ab.de/learngerman
Credit system and grading
A full-time workload is 30 ECTS credits per 
semester. Grades are awarded from 1,0 (highest) 
to 5,0 (lowest) with 4,0 as the minimum passing 
grade. Some courses are evaluated on a pass / 
fail grading system.
Erasmus+ and exchange students will receive 
credits for all successfully completed courses and 
all obtained credits will be listed on a transcript 
of records. Students can download the transcript 
of records themselves, and it will also be sent 
directly to the home institution.

【第10頁】
Fee
No fees will be charged by Aschaffenburg UAS, 
but all students have to pay the semester fee. In 
Germany, the Studentenwerk maintains a range 
of services such as the campus dining hall, 
the halls of residence, or counselling services. 
According to the Bavarian Higher Education Act, 
all students are to pay a small service fee for 
the administration of these services – currently 
70 EUR (as of March 2025).
Nomination and application 
Exchange students are nominated by their home 
university before they apply at Aschaffenburg UAS 
using an online application form. 
 www.th-ab.de/apply-online
Nomination / application deadlines
Winter semester: 20 May / 1 June
Summer semester: 20 November / 1 December
Classes
Students are encouraged to organise their 
learning in a responsible and self-regulated way. 
Attendance is not compulsory for most classes. 
At the same time, active participation is expected. 
Please:
   do ask if you have questions,
   contribute whenever there is an opportunity,
    get in contact with your German classmates 
and do not be afraid of taking the initiative.
Often, so called Tutorien are offered – additional 
classes where students help you grasp the 
material. Tutorien are announced by your 
professors and on campus.
10

【第11頁】
Aschaffenburg is a medium-sized city with a 
population of around 70,000 and lies on the 
River Main. The city is famous for its municipal 
museums, its interesting and varied cultural 
programme and a wide variety of cafés, bars and 
clubs. Annual festivals such as the Afro-Caribbean 
Festival, the Volksfest and the big Stadtfest 
attract visitors from all over the country. They are 
permanent highlights in the city’s event calendar 
and popular among young and old alike.
Main campus in Aschaffenburg
Situated between large conurbations and areas of 
unspoilt nature, Aschaffenburg is often described 
as a city where people can enjoy life to the fullest.
 www.tourist-aschaffenburg.de/en/home.html
© Foto: stock.adobe.de – Aquarius 11

【第12頁】
Campus services and facilities 
Aschaffenburg UAS is heavily invested in ensuring 
that students and staff have access to everything 
they need to succeed in their studies and work. 
Learning resources and personal support have 
placed Aschaffenburg on the map as one of 
Germany’s top universities for overall student 
satisfaction. 
The International Office  is located in building 1, 
rooms E11 – E13, and is the first point of 
contact for incoming students and staff from 
abroad. If you have any questions of a personal, 
administrative or social nature, please contact 
us. Similarly, if you have a disability or chronic 
illness and need special support, please let us 
know – we can help you apply for disadvantage 
compensation.

【第14頁】
Housing
The Studierendenwerk runs two halls of residence 
on and near the campus, renting out furnished 
single rooms in shared apartments as well 
as furnished single apartments. Wheelchair 
accessible apartments are available. Please 
apply by 15 June (winter semester) / 15 January 
(summer semester). For a small fee and upon 
request, the Studierendenwerk also rents 
household packages that include bedding. 
 www.studentenwerk-wuerzburg.de/en/
A room in the halls of residence is not 
guaranteed. This is why we recommend that 
you look for private accommodation as well. 
In Germany, many students live in flat shares 
(Wohngemeinschaft / WG). Each tenant has their 
own room but the kitchen and bathroom are 
shared. The cost of electricity, water, internet and 
telephone is also shared. For a furnished room in 
a flat share, you can expect to pay EUR 500–700. 
Please check the following websites for rooms  
to let:
www
                     
www
 www.wg-gesucht.de/en/  www.studenten-wg.de 
In addition, there are some private providers 
of halls of residence in Aschaffenburg. They 
offer furnished rooms as well as rooms without 
furniture.

Student life 
Joining university sports (Hochschulsport) is 
a great way to make friends and meet local 
students while studying with us. The programme 
usually includes a mix of exercise classes and 
current trend sports, all taught by experienced 
trainers. Everyone is welcome to participate, 
from beginners to advanced athletes. In general, 
participation is free of charge and possible 
without prior registration.
There are also various student organisations on 
campus. The Studentenvertretung is the student 
representation at Aschaffenburg UAS. They 
meet biweekly and discuss issues of student 
welfare as well as organise events and activities. 
As an exchange student you have the same 
opportunities as our degree-seeking students to 
join the Studentenvertretung or any of our other 
student organisations, such as Rolling Students, 
Economics, or Students meet Real Estate e. V.

The Federal Republic of Germany is located 
directly in the heart of Europe and extends from 
the Baltic Sea in the north to the Alps in the south. 
It is not big in size but offers one of the highest 
standards of living in the world as well as diverse 
art and culture, and it is well-known for its high-
quality products. With its 84 million inhabitants 
it has the largest population of all EU member 
states.
Living and studying in Germany
Germany is often seen as a byword for stability. 
It is a parliamentary democracy and its citizens 
trust in fair elections and the rule of law – it is 
a safe country where you can travel freely and 
feel secure. A German proverb claims that ‘five 
minutes ahead of time is the German punctuality’. 
Germans are undoubtedly dependent and reliable. 
At the same time, German society is diverse, 
colourful and cosmopolitan. To most Germans, 
equality is an important value – living free from 
worry and with equal opportunities regardless of 
gender, race, sexual orientation, or religion.
The country is also considered an economic 
giant. Its machinery and electrical equipment 
are known for their high quality and durability 
and the country is one of the largest automobile 
producers in the world. While Germany can be 
proud of the richness of its economy, perhaps 
even more notable is its richness of human life – 
people have opportunities and choices. Germany 
has consistently been ranked among the best 
countries to live in by the Human Development 
Report.
 www.deutschland.de/en

【第18頁】
While English-taught modules take place almost 
exclusively on the main campus in Aschaffenburg, 
there are also two smaller locations in town and 
a campus in Miltenberg, which is located about 
40 km from Aschaffenburg.
Aschaffenburg UAS is a research-intensive 
university of applied sciences with special focus 
on intelligent systems, materials, information 
management and structural transformation. 
Within international research consortia as well as 
in intensive cooperation with local partners, our 
scientists strive to foster innovation in business 
and society. 
Other campuses and facilities
In the Centre for Scientific Services and Transfer 
(ZeWiS) Aschaffenburg UAS strengthens its 
cooperation with the regional industry. Located in 
Obernburg – halfway between our main campus 
in Aschaffenburg and our campus in Miltenberg – 
ZeWiS maintains more than 1,000 square meters 
of laboratory space for application-oriented 
research and transfer. 
 www.th-ab.de/en/research/collaborate/students
18

【第19頁】
Practicalities
Visa
EU and EFTA nationals do not require a visa to 
enter Germany. If you are not an EU national, 
please contact the German Embassy or German 
Consulate in your country of residence to check 
visa regulations as well as residence permit 
regulations prior to travelling to Germany. Do not 
enter with a tourist visa. 
 www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en
Arrival 
Aschaffenburg is located around 40 km from 
Frankfurt, where a major international airport 
is located, making it easy to reach the area by 
plane. From “FRA Frankfurt Airport” you can take 
a train to “Aschaffenburg Hbf”. There are also two 
smaller train stations in town: Aschaffenburg Süd  
and Aschaffenburg Hochschule, which is located 
next to Aschaffenburg UAS.
 www.bahn.com/en
© Foto: stock.adobe.de – dietwalther 19

【第20頁】
Registration in town
All students have to register their place of 
residence within two weeks of their arrival at 
the town hall’s Residents’ Registration Office 
(Einwohnermeldeamt). After the registration 
you will receive a confirmation called 
Meldebescheinigung that is often required to open 
a German bank account. 
Please bring:
    your passport / ID card,
    your certificate of enrolment,
    your rental contract and documents 
(Wohnungsgeberbescheinigung).
Insurance
It is mandatory as a student to have health 
insurance cover for your entire stay in Germany. 
EU and EFTA nationals are entitled to medical 
treatment with their European Health Insurance 
Card. Students from outside EU/EFTA countries 
should sign up for statutory or private health 
insurance. We recommend taking out a policy 
with a German statutory health insurance 
company. These institutions offer special prices 
for students — approx. 130 EUR / month for 
health and long-term care insurance.
In addition, we recommend taking out personal 
liability insurance (Haftpflichtversicherung). 
Although it is not compulsory, it covers unintentional 
damage to a third party or a third party’s property.
20

【第21頁】
Buddy programme
As an international student, you will be matched 
with a local “buddy” who will help you get settled 
in Aschaffenburg. Your buddy is a full-time 
student at Aschaffenburg UAS and will meet you 
upon arrival, show you around and help you with 
practical matters, such as registration or opening 
a bank account. During the semester, the buddies 
will organise social events and trips, and answer 
social questions throughout your stay.
Welcome Weeks
Prior to the start of the semester, the International 
Office organises two (compulsory) Welcome 
Weeks. You will have the chance to learn some 
German, clear all administrative milestones, and 
participate in various events and activities. This is 
a great opportunity to settle in, meet new people 
and make some friends.
Cost of living
Prices in Germany are in line with the EU average. 
The German government estimates the average 
expenditure for students to be approx. EUR 934 
a month, which includes accommodation, food, 
study materials, leisure, and transport. There are 
many generous grant and scholarship schemes 
that can help to cover your cost of living during 
your stay. 
 www.daad.de/en 
Licence fee
Every household in Germany is required to pay 
a licence fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) of 18.36 EUR /
month for public service broadcasting. The fee is 
subject to the principle of solidarity. It is relatively 
small because everyone pays regardless of   
actual media use. 
 www.rundfunkbeitrag.de/welcome


【第22頁】
Public and regional holidays
In Germany, there are various public holidays. 
Some apply throughout Germany and some only 
in some federal states. Below you can find an 
overview of the public holidays in Germany and 
Bavaria. Please be aware that shops are closed 
on public holidays.
Emergency phone numbers
Police: 110
Emergency medical services / fire brigade: 112
If you do not have any life-threatening pains or 
illnesses, it is common to make an appointment 
to see a general practitioner (Hausarzt). They can 
assess whether an illness or injury ought to be 
treated by a specialist, in which case he or she 
writes a referral.

【第1頁】
    
 
 
 
Fact Sheet on Student Exchange Program 
Academic year 2026/2027 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Contact information 
Name of university Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences (HKA) 
(Hochschule Karlsruhe (HKA)) 
Coordinating office International Office 
Mailing address Moltkestraße 30, 76133 Karlsruhe, Germany 
Contact information Incoming Student Advisors  
 Ms. Lea Scholz + Ms. Anna Tillhon 
Email: incoming@h-ka.de 
Tel.: +49 (0)721 – 925 1086 
         +49 (0)721 – 925 1141 
 Outgoing Student Advisor  
 Mr. Hannes Schwarz 
E-Mail: hannes.schwarz@h-ka.de 
Tel.: +49 (0)721 – 925 1085 
 Deputy Director International Office  
 Ms. Silke Neureuther 
Email: silke.neureuther@h-ka.de 
Tel.: +49 (0)721 – 925 1081 
 HKA International Program (English taught courses)  
 Ms. Anja Voges + Ms. Tatiana Shakhtyr 
Email: internationalprogram@h-ka.de 
 (Contact person for Erasmus-OLA) 
Tel.: +49 (0)721 – 925 2506 
Erasmus code D KARLSRU05 
Website https://www.h-ka.de/en/io 
General information 
Academic calendar Winter Semester 2026/27 
September 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 
Summer Semester 2027 
March 1, 2027 – August 31, 2027 
Welcome and orientation phase September 11 – 27, 2026 Feb 26 – March 14, 2027 
Preparatory intensive German 
language course September 14 – 25, 2026 March 1 – March 12, 2027 
Teaching period  September 28, 2026 – January 22, 2027 
March 15 – July 2, 2027 
 
 


【第2頁】
Fact Sheet 2026/27 www.h-ka.de  
 
Examinations January 25 – February 12, 2027 July 05 – July 23, 2027 
Holidays / 
Semester Breaks 
December 22, 2026 – January 6, 2027 
(Christmas) 
April 03 – April 07, 2026 (Easter) 
June 09 – June 15, 2026 (Whitsun) 
Link to academic calendar https://www.h-ka.de/en/about-hka/news-events/academic-calendar/semester- 
dates#c39192 
Student workload The normal workload for full-time students is 30 ECTS credits per semester. 
Application + nomination deadline May 15 November 15 
Application procedure  Via online portal. Information at: https://www.h-ka.de/en/exchange-students 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Application process 
Requested application documents: 
• Learning agreement listing the course units that they wish to take1 
• Transcripts of Records obtained in previous years of study 
• Copy of passport 
If a student intends to do a thesis project at HKA or an internship in industry, a short 
description of the intended subject area of the thesis / the internship is required. 
Applications sent by post cannot be considered. 
Incomplete applications cannot be considered. 
It is very important that the applicants spell their full name as it appears on their 
passport, and that they attach a copy of their passport. 
Any delay in sending the documents may cause problems in finding accommodation. 
Students who need a visa should bear in mind that the visa application process may 
take up to ten weeks. We therefore strongly recommend that those students submit 
their application as early as possible, and no later than May 15 / November 15. 
Once we have received the complete application, we will forward it to the relevant 
Faculty for their assessment. This may take up to 6 weeks. As soon as the faculty has 
agreed to accept a student, we will issue the invitation letter. An electronic copy, which 
can be used for a visa application, will be sent to the student by e-mail. 
 
Language requirement 
For courses taught in German, a minimum language competency at CEFR (Common 
European Framework of Reference for Languages) B2 level is required. Likewise, for the 
International Program a minimum English language competency at CEFR B2 level is 
required. 
Students who do not fulfill the language requirement cannot be accepted. 
 
Can students extend their 
exchange period? 
Yes, but this would be subject to the approval of the home and host universities. 
Students may extend their stay for another study semester or for an internship in 
industry, provided they have been successful in finding a placement for themselves. 
HKA will assist exchange students in finding a place, but cannot provide internships 
itself. 
 
Activities or services available to 
exchange students 
• Access to campus facilities including library, student canteen, etc. 
• Buddy-program: buddies will help in administrative matters in the first weeks 
• Events and excursions for international students are offered at modest prices 
• Free limited semester ticket for the Karlsruhe Public Transport System KVV with the 
option to purchase a full semester ticket with a substantial student discount 
 
 
1 Note that here are courses for which, according to examination rules, only pass/fail grades are given. 
For information about German courses consult the module descriptions for the individual degree programs at https://www.h-ka.de/en/study. 
For HKA International Program courses there will be a remark in the Learning Agreement. 

【第3頁】
Fact Sheet 2026/27 www.h-ka.de  
 
Course-related information for exchange students 
Online course information https://www.h-ka.de/en/exchange-students 
Course schedule/timetable Will be provided upon arrival. 
Medium of instruction and 
assessment 
The medium of instruction and assessment for courses offered within the HKA 
International Program is English. For other courses it is German, unless specified 
otherwise. 
Minimum and maximum number of 
credits to be taken per semester 
Maximum number of ECTS credit points per semester: 30. Depending on approval by 
the sending institution, exchange students can take fewer credits, but not more. 
Are students allowed to take cross- 
faculty modules? 
Yes, subject to approval by the faculties involved. It is the student’s responsibility to 
make sure that this does not result in timetable clashes. 
 
Level of courses 
Exchange students normally take courses according to their academic level at their 
home institution. Advanced bachelor students may be eligible to take master’s courses, 
provided they meet the respective academic requirements. 
 
 
Language classes 
German Language Intensive Course starting approx. two weeks before lectures start 
(levels A 1 – B2.2). German language classes are also offered during the semester (level 
A 1 – B 2.2). All German language classes are free of charge for exchange students. For 
higher levels, students will be assisted in finding courses at other institutions. 
Other language courses including English, French and Spanish are offered to interested 
students free of charge at the HKA’s Foreign Language Institute (IFS). 
 
Transcripts 
HKA’s International Office will receive the official transcripts approx. 6- 7 weeks after 
end of examination period and will send them on to the sending institutions 
International Office by e-mail and, if requested, also in paper form. 
Accommodation 
 
 
Is university accommodation 
available for exchange students? 
There are 2 options: 
1. Students can apply for university accommodation directly at the Student Services 
Information: https://www.sw-ka.de/en/wohnen/ 
2. The International Office has a limited quota of rooms in student hostels. Students 
will receive information on how to apply for such a room with their invitation letter. 
These rooms can only be rented for one semester. 
Is university accommodation 
guaranteed? No, unfortunately we cannot guarantee it. 
Is accommodation available over 
semester breaks? University accommodation (option 2) can only be rented for a complete semester. 
Website for information on 
accommodation  For more information about accommodation: https://www.h-ka.de/en/accommodation 
Visa requirements 
Are exchange students required to 
obtain a student visa? 
Depends on nationality; information at www.auswaertiges- 
amt.de/EN/EinreiseUndAufenthalt/03_Visabestimmungen/Visabestimmungen_node.h 
tml 
Are exchange students allowed to 
work? 
Exchange students are expected to have a full study workload. In order for students to 
get the most out of their exchange academically, we cannot recommend working. 
However, they are usually allowed to work a maximum of 20h per week. 

【第4頁】
Fact Sheet 2026/27 www.h-ka.de  
 
Arrival / Orientation program 
Recommended arrival dates Winter Semester 
An orientation will take place the week 
before German intensive courses start 
To guarantee smooth enrolment we 
highly recommend that students arrive 
two weeks before lectures start. 
Summer Semester 
An orientation will take place the week 
before German intensive courses start 
To guarantee smooth enrolment we highly 
recommend that students arrive two weeks 
before lectures start. 
Is an airport pick-up service 
available? 
No, there isn’t. The train connections between Frankfurt airport and Karlsruhe are 
excellent, with trains running hourly during the daytime. 
Insurance 
Are exchange students required to 
purchase insurance? 
Yes. It is mandatory for enrollment. Since Winter Semester 2020/2021, there are new 
health insurance requirements for students under 30! 
1. Private health insurances will need to be approved by German statuary health insurance 
2. Students need a full coverage health insurance, including a nursing care 
insurance 
3. Valid health insurance is a prerequisite for enrolment and has to be taken care of 
before arrival. The cost is approx. € 120 per month. 
Estimated expenses in local currency 
(The estimated costs are for reference only. Actual expenses may vary from person to person.) 
• € 115 contribution fee for student services (Studierendenwerk) per semester 
• € 10 one-off fee for the campus card 
• Approx. € 390 for accommodation per month 
• Approx. € 140 for insurance per month 
• Approx. € 190 for public transport (depending on the student’s place of residence) per semester 
• Approx. € 90 for meals in the student canteen per month 
It is not possible to transfer payments in advance. Students must make sure they have sufficient financial means for meeting 
the costs above and living expenses once they are in Karlsruhe (details will be given by the International Office). 
 
Scholarship program for exchange students: https://www.bw-stipendium.de/en/ 
Contact person at HKA: Hannes Schwarz: hannes.schwarz@h-ka.de (students have to be nominated) 
German grading system 
Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences uses the following grading scheme: 
• 1,0 – 1,5 (Very good) 
• 1,6 – 2,5 (Good) 
• 2,6 – 3,5 (Satisfactory) 
• 3,6 – 4,0 (Sufficient) 
• 4,1 – 5,0 (non-sufficient / fail) 
Some courses at HKA are not graded and simply evaluated with “pass” or “fail”.

Transcript of Records
I want to stay longer!
Downloads and links
Before your arrival
Which courses can I take?
As an exchange student you have the opportunity to attend courses in German or in English and to receive credit at home for your achievements from one or two exchange semesters at HKA. Courses from our regular degree programs, which are usually taught in German, can be found
here
.
You will find a large selection of courses taught in English at our International Program:
Winter Semester
and
Summer Semester
.
For both languages, a language level of B2 (European Framework of Reference) is required.
By taking a German language course (two-week intensive course before the start of the semester and/or semester course) you can acquire 5 ECTS points.
When and how do I apply?
After your home university has nominated you for the exchange semester at HKA and you have agreed on a so-called Learning Agreement, you apply at HKA via the
application portal
of the International Office. The application deadline is November 15 for the summer semester and May 15 for the winter semester. If you need a visa, you should allow approximately 10 weeks for this and apply in due time.
Please ask your home university coordinator for advice on the exact application procedure and your learning agreement. Important: Some courses at HKA are not graded with a mark, but with pass/fail.
Which documents do I need?
For your application:
Filled-in learning agreement; Erasmus Students can send their Online Learning Agreement (OLA) via the EWP-dashboard instead. In that case, please just upload a document stating “OLA via EWP dashboard” in the online portal. (The normal semester workload is 30 credit points (CP) according to ECTS, in accordance with your home university, you can take less CP but not more).
current transcript of records / transcript of grades from your university
for thesis or internship semester: short description of the planned topic
copy of your passport
Other important documents:
Visa: an overview of visa regulations can be found
here
. Soon after your application you will receive an invitation letter which you should use to start the visa process as soon as possible. We collected some helpful
here
and
this page
has proofen to be very helpful.
Since recently,
proof of insurance
is a mandatory part of enrolment at German universities. Therefore this needs to be taken care of before your arrival as well (by July for winter semester or January for summer semester).
Students with disabilities or chronic illnesses can find information on disadvantage compensation (e.g. for exams) or accessibility
here
. Please contact the International Office as early as possible - ideally already during the application process - to apply for compensation for disadvantages.
What about accommodation?
We strongly recommend starting your room search as early as possible.
On this site
you'll find a lot of helpful links.
After your arrival
Registering in Karlsruhe
Everybody has to register with the city of Karlsruhe (Bürgerbüro/Einwohnermeldeamt) within two weeks after moving into his or her apartment/room. Please note that you also have to notify the Bürgerbüro/Einwohnermeldeamt every time you change your address in Germany. To get registered you need to make an appointment
here
(you might have to reload the page). Choose “Meldewesen”- Zuzug nach Karlsruhe" (the first option under "Meldewesen"), click "Weiter", in the calendar you'll see the next available appointments. You can do the registration at any office (K8 is closest to the University). Confirm your choice ("Termin wählen") and  fill in your information and click on "Weiter".
You will receive a confirmation mail with a booking number. Keep that number safe and  and be sure to cancel the appointment if you are unable to go! You should be at the appoinment 15 Minutes early.
You will need the following documents:
Your passport
Wohnungsgeberbestätigung / Landlord certificate (This form has to be filled out and signed by your landlord, you can find it under
Formulare
. Unfortunately, all forms are only available in German).
This is not your rental contract!
If applicable: your residence permit or visa
At the end you will receive a Registration Confirmation - make sure to keep this document safe!
Getting your residence permit
All non-EU exchange students
either need to have a visa that covers the whole exchange period or a valid residence permit for studying purposes. This means that if your visa expires before the end of your exchange stay, you will need to apply for a residence permit for studying purposes before the expiry date of your visa.
You will need to submit the following documents (copies) to the Ausländerbehörde (foreigners office):
copy of your current visa for Germany (if applicable)
copy of your passport
proof of sufficient funds to cover all expenses during your stay in Germany (at least 992 € monthly, e.g. blocked bank account or official statement of your scholarship)
"Immatrikulationsbescheinigung" (Proof of enrollment)
proof of health insurance (confirmation issued by your insurance provider)
You should also compile and upload:
confirmation of your registration as a resident of the city of Karlsruhe (see
above
)
copy of your rental contract
any further confirmation that can support your application (e.g. confirmation about the extension of your exchange semester)
You can fill in the application online
here
(choose option 1 - residence permit for training) and upload all your documents there. Make sure to note down your Application-Number at the end and that you really receive a confirmation mail.
The processing of applications currently takes about 10 weeks
, so it is important to submit your application as early as possible. You will receive their decision via post or e-mail. After receiving their decision, you can make an
appointment
to submit the biometric data (fingerprints and photo - choose "Abgabe biometrischer Daten"). At this appointment they will order your new electronic residence permit. The cost of the permit is around 100€.
Should you not be able to submit everything via the link above, you can send your documents via mail (as one pdf) by email to
abh
spam prevention
@oa.karlsruhe.de
. You will need to add the filled in application form (click
here
and choose "Antrag auf Erteilung einer Aufenthaltserlaubnis" under "Formulare"). Make sure that your application is complete and save the automatically sent confirmation of receipt afterwards. Please be aware that sending the application via e-mail can lead to longer processing times.
General information about Karlsruhe
Check this
website
to learn about public transport system, recreational activities, doctor offices and more!
Before leaving Karlsruhe
De-registering from HKA
Once your stay at HKA is unfortunately coming to an end, we kindly ask you to request your de-registration (Exmatrikulation) from HKA to avoid any issues after your return. You will also need your "Exmatrikulationsbescheinigung" if you want to study at any German university again.
In order to ex-matriculate please get the signature from the library and send the signed
request for exmatriculation
via e-mail to
incoming
spam prevention
@h-ka.de
or upload it on the Hisinone portal. A few days later, you can download the de-registration certificate on Hisinone. You can also send the form before your departure, as the deregistration will only take effect after August 31st and has no influence on the current semester.
De-registering from the city
You have to notify the city of Karlsruhe that you are leaving the city. This can be done from one week before leaving until two weeks afterwards and is in your best interest because you also want to de-register from paying the Rundfunkbeitrag and avoid issues, should you ever travel to Germany again.
The de-regsitration can be done online, via post or in Person. To de-register from the city open
Onlineanträge "Ins Ausland abmelden"
and either make an appointment or download the form to send it via post.
To de-register from paying the Rundfunkbeitrag you can simply follow the steps
on their website
(again - this is all in German).
You should also inform your German health insurance provider a few days before you leave, so that you do not have to pay more than you need.
Transcript of Records
You can download your transcript of records
here
. Choose “Meine Funktionen” - click “Prüfungsverwaltung” on the left side - click “Bescheinigungen“ - choose the document/report you need (“Notenspiegel” = contains all courses you took, also the ones you failed. Only available in German | ECTS-Leistungsnachweis (Transcript of records) = does not include failed courses; comes with English translation). Some courses need to be added manually for exchange students. Therefore, the transcript is sometimes not complete even after the deadline to enter grades. Should you encounter any issues with your transcript, please contact us. Around mid-August or the beginning of March your transcript will also be send to your coordinator at your home university.
I want to stay longer
We are happy to know that you are enjoying your time at HKA and decided to extend your stay for a second semester.
Please inform us in the International Office at the latest by the end of June or the beginning of January, should you wish to extend your stay. You also need your home university's approval and please ask them to send a confirmation email to HKA's International Office.
Please send us the following documents via mail:
Enrollment certificate from your home university for the period you want to extend your stay (Please notice that you need to be enrolled at your home university for the entire duration of your stay at HKA)
A new learning agreement signed and stamped from your home university or a confirmation about your internship
Important: For your second semester at HKA, you must pay the student services fee of 108.70 EUR within the re-registration period.Don't forget to inform your health insurance provider in time and, if necessary, also the immigration office to extend your residence permit.

International Office DHBW Loerrach V1.

3 
 
 
Visa: Non-EU citizens have to obtain a Student Visa! 
(Exception: Non-EU citizens with residence permit in EU) 
Visa applications to the German Embassy or Consulate 
should be submitted well in time (8-12 weeks before 
semester start or earlier) after receipt of Letter of 
acceptance from DHBW Loerrach. A Schengen Visa is 
recommended. 
Please inform yourself about Visa Formalities and check if you 
meet the Visa requirements before you apply. 
 
Registration at the Federal 
Office of Migration and 
Refugees (BAMF) 
Non-EU citizens without Student Visa but with residence permit 
in EU must be reported to the BAMF with complete documents: 
• Residence permit from the first EU country 
• Recognized valid passport 
• Evidence of participation in a Union or multilateral mobility 
program or the agreement between the universities

(= 6 months) 
     13€ Studierendenschaftsbeitrag per student per semester

mandatory:

to a third person, equipment or at their accommodation, 
regardless of whether the damages were caused through 
negligence or otherwise. 
ONLY GERMAN STATUTORY CIVIL LIABILITY INSURANCE

a further private insurance is recommended.

against loss through accidental bodily injury to the insured. 
Contact us. 
 
Travel cancellation insurance 
recommended: 
A travel cancellation insurance covers all possible travel

 must have confirmed accommodation before arrival.

flatshares & roommates

Expenses: Please calculate all occurring expenses for your stay including 
flights and living expenses generously. Be aware that average 
living expenses per month in Germany are at minimum 1,000 
€.. A credit card is recommended. 
 
 
Recommended airports:  EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse (nearest), Zurich, Frankfurt,     
  Stuttgart

Laptop is essential.  
 
Psychotherapeutic Counseling: Psychotherapeutic counseling is available for students at all 
 DHBW university locations, offering confidential individual 
 support and workshops on successful studying.  
 SwFR - Psychotherapeutic Counselling 
 
Psychological Video Consultation for DHBW students available

confidential setting. These coaching and counseling sessions 
are free of charge and confidential.

The living costs in Loerrach are estimated 
between 1.000 – 1.500 Euros per month.

activities, travel and so on. Please make 
sure to have sufficient money available to 
spend the time here without financial

Once you have arrived in Loerrach, you 
have to register at the City Hall. The 
following documents are necessary for 
the registration: your passport, your visa 
(if you have one), the completed 
registration form, the rental contract. You 
have to inform the City Hall every time 
you move to a another place in Loerrach. 
That means that you also have to 
de-register again when you return to your 
home country, after your semester at our 
university is over.
BAMF REGISTRATION
Registration at Federal Office for Migration 
and Refugees (BAMF) for students from 
countries outside the European Union, 
who wish to stay up to 360 days in 
Germany for study purposes:
If you already hold a residence title issued 
by another Member State for study 
purposes, you do not require a German 
residence title, but your residence title 
must be valid for the entire duration of 
your stay in Germany.
The German higher education institution 
must submit prior notification of your 
intended stay to the Federal Office for 
Migration and Refugees. This notification 
should be provided as soon as it becomes 
known that you intend to study in 
Germany. Full notification absolutely must 
be received no later than 30 days prior to 
your entering Germany.
The Federal Office for Migration and 
Refugees will issue you with a certificate 
confirming your entitlement to stay in 
Germany.

BADEN-WUERTTEMBERG
Loerrach is situated in the federal state of 
Baden-Wuerttemberg, which ranks among 
Europe‘s leaders in technology and 
maintains long traditions of innovation 
and creativity.
Impressive brands such as Porsche and 
Mercedes-Benz have headquarters and 
museums located in the region. The 
capital, Stuttgart, is home to one of the 
largest zoos and botanical gardens in 
Europe. Stuttgart is a popular destination 
for our students due to its nearby location 
and entertainment possibilities. 
The people in Baden-Wuerttemberg 
benefit of an outstanding quality of life. 
People feel at home, enjoying a rich 
beautiful landscape and a lively internati-
onal arts and culture scene. They profit 
from the community’s outstanding 
environmental values.
With its 11 million inhabitants, Baden- 
Württemberg is the third largest of the 16 
German federal states. Nearly 1.2 million 
residents are of non-German origin, 
mostly Turkish, Greek and Italian. 
Baden-Württemberg also enjoys one the 
lowest unemployment rates of any 
German federal state. This makes it a 
perfect location for students, who want to 
build their careers. 
LOERRACH
Loerrach is a small city in the south of 
Germany near the borders to Switzerland 
and France. This contributes to the 
outstanding character of the region. 
Loerrach has many attractions like the 
ruins of Roetteln Castle from the 11th 
Century. This castle is situated on a hilltop 
overlooking Loerrach and the valley of the 
river Wiese. Parkschwimmbad, a huge 
outdoor swim area, is another large 
attraction of Loerrach’s, with a wave 
machine, water slides, diving platforms 
and an exercise pool. It’s great to be there 
on a bright day together with friends. 
Besides Loerrach has an impressive 
concert hall, the Burghof, the picturesque 
river Wiese and many large companies.

Programme Students
Erasmus study abroad experiences, student exchanges under a partnership/student exchange agreement (incl. the Coimbra Group Student Exchange Network and the Swiss European Mobility Programme), holders of scholarships or grants provided by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), Fulbright, FGAC; please enquire about other programmes.
If your home university does not have a partnership agreement with the University of Würzburg and you have not been selected for a scholarship programme, under certain conditions it is possible to spend an exchange semester at the University of Würzburg as a so-called
freemover
.
1. Application an nomination via your home university
You will have to apply directly to your home university/the scholarship or grant sponsor.
If you are selected for participation, your home university/sponsor* will nominate you to us.
Deadlines for nominations to the University of Würzburg:
30 April for winter intake
30 November for summer intake
Find out what
language requirements
you will have to meet to qualify for admission as an exchange student.
AFTER your home university/sponsor has nominated you to us, we will email you a link that will take you to our online registration form.
*Some sponsors do not contact the host universities with nominations. If that is the case for your sponsor, please email us at
exchange-international@uni-wuerzburg.de
before the deadline for nominations has passed and let us have a letter from your sponsor confirming that they have awarded the scholarship or grant to you.
2. Fill registration form
AFTER your home university/sponsor has nominated you to us, we will email you a link that will take you to our online registration form.
Deadlines for online registration
15 June for winter intake
15 January for summer intake
Please contact us if you are unable to meet this deadline.
Please register as soon as possible after you receive our email.
Please note
The application deadlines for rooms in
student residences
are 15 June for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester! You will NOT have to supply a letter of admission when you apply for a room in a student residence.
Please be aware that there is a special application process in place for exchange students. We will send you the relevant instructions after we have received your nomination.
You will have to attach the following documents when registering online:
An enrolment certificate issued by your home university
A transcript of records issued by your home university that documents your academic achievements to date
Proof of your proficiency in the German language (if you are not holding an official German language certificate, you can ask one of the German teachers at your home university to issue you with a letter to confirm that you have the required German language skills;
template letter
)
Proof of your proficiency in the English language (if you are not holding an official English language certificate, you can ask one of the English teachers at your home university to issue you with a letter to confirm that you have the required English language skills;
template letter
)
Only required if you are doing an exchange programme other than Erasmus
: If you are doing a student exchange at the University of Würzburg under a partnership agreement: a list of the courses you want to take at the University of Würzburg (course selection list;
template and more information
)
Information regarding language certificates
We do not accept OLS test certificates as proof of your language skills.
3. Admission to the University of Würzburg as an programme student
Once we have received your online registration, the team at the International Office Incoming will review the information and documents you have supplied and will then issue you with a letter of admission to the University of Würzburg as an exchange student. We usually start sending out our letters of admission in June (for winter intake) or, respectively, in December (for summer intake). They are sent by email. Along with your letter of admission, you will receive more information about your stay at the University of Würzburg.
4. Enrolment
You can enrol through the online platform of the University of Würzburg
WueStudy
. You will receive all the information needed on your Admission Letter. Feel free to contact our staff and our
tutors
if you need a helping hand. You will receive your student ID card and semester ticket a few days after enrolment.
Further information for enrolment
Fact sheet for exchange students

Language proficiency
The main language of instruction is German. But you will find also courses in English in the faculties.As an exchange student, you should have sufficient language proficiency to follow the courses. It is not necessary for most subjects, however, to have a specific level of proficiency in German to be admitted as an exchange student.

If you wish to earn ECTS credits at the University of Würzburg, you should be able to demonstrate a B1-level of proficiency (exception: courses at the Language Center)

Liste der geplanten Kurse 
List of planned courses 
 
Die Kursliste ist nicht verbindlich, sondern ermöglicht der Universität Würzburg vorab einen 
Überblick über die von Ihnen eingeplanten Kurse. 
Erasmus-Studierende, die ein Learning Agreement für die Dauer ihres Aufenthalts an unserer 
Hochschule abschließen müssen, brauchen dieses Dokument nicht auszufüllen. 
Diese Liste ersetzt nicht die Registrierung für die Kurse in WueStudy. 
The courses listed below are not compulsory, they are only meant to give the University of Würzburg 
an overview of the courses planned by the student. 
Erasmus students who have to submit a Learning Agreement for the duration of their stay at our 
University do not have to fill in this document. 
This list does not replace the the registration for the courses in WueStudy. 
 
Nutzen Sie für die Kurswahl das Vorlesungsverzeichnis des vergangenen 
Winter/Sommersemesters in WueStudy und tragen Sie Ihre Präferenzen hier ein. Bitte 
beachten Sie, dass es zu Änderungen im Vorlesungsverzeichnis kommen kann und Sie Ihre 
Kurswahl ggf. nach Ihrer Ankunft ändern müssen. Die Änderungen müssen dem International 
Office Incoming nicht mitgeteilt werden. 
You can search for courses in WueStudy via the course catalogue of the previous winter/summer 
semester and list your preferred courses on this form. Please note that if changes are made to the 
course catalogue, you may have to change your course selection. The International Office Incoming

Tips:
In the
module descriptions and handbooks
, you will find additional information, also available in English.
Please contact the academic coordinator; they can recommend suitable courses for you.
You can also use the previous year's schedule as a reference
1. Open the online course catalogue
Open the
course catalogue
.
Important:
Choose the right Semester! You can use our
video tutorials
(course management) to become familiar with our course catalogue.
Tip:
Always choose the programme with the higher number of ECTS. All courses included in programmes with fewer credits are also included in this programme.
2. Important hints
You’re also allowed to take courses for students of all subjects ("Veranstaltungen für Hörer/-innen aller Fakultäten")
(e.g. for language courses, etc.).
To find English taught courses, please use the Advanced Search function and select English as the teaching language.
You will be admitted to the major specified in your application (ERASMUS according to the bilateral agreement), but as an exchange student you can also attend courses in other subjects. However, in some courses it could be required to have previous knowledge of the subject. You can ask the lecturer.
Language courses start with a placement test. With the help of this placement test you will be assigned to a course that corresponds to your language level. This means that the course level you specify in your Learning Agreement might change after the test.
3. Tips to understand the terms used
By clicking on a course, you get further information. This table will help you to understand the terms used.
4. Complete the Learning Agreement and register for courses
Complete your Learning Agreement with the chosen courses. Changes to the chosen courses in the Learning Agreement are possible after arrival in Würzburg at any time and on previous arrangement with the Coordinator (“changes to the original Learning Agreement”).
At the University of Würzburg, the Learning Agreements will be signed by the
departmental coordinators
.
You know if you need a Learning Agreement for your home university. If your home university doesn’t need one, the University of Würzburg doesn’t need it either.

Enrolment & Semester Fees
Enrolment & Semester Fees
Online enrolment/ online registration
1. Online-Enrolment
You can do the
online enrolment
for the winter term 2026/27  starting from July  22st via
online portal for enrolment
of the University of Würzburg.
2. Hand in documents
As part of the online enrolment you have to
upload on the portal Wuestudy the following documents:
Letter of Acceptance / Letter of Admission
Proof of payment of the semester fee (see below)
Copy of your passport
Kindly send
by email
to the International Students Office the
PDF of your Online Enrolment
so we can proceed your enrolment.
Contact a german statutory
health insurance
as a
digital confirmation
about your health insurance status is requiered as part of your enrolment.
As soon as we received and checked your documents we will complete your enrolment and inform you when your student card is ready to be picked up.
With the
student card
, you can:
Use all local
public transportation
in Würzburg. You can find further information about the semester ticket and a plan of the routes for which your ticket is valid
on
Studierendenwerk's website
.
Make cashless payments in the
cafeterias
and copy and print stations at the University of Würzburg;
Borrow library items from the
university libraries.
Semester Fee
There are no study fees at the University of Würzburg.
All students must, however, pay a semester fee of
€ 182,10
before they can be enrolled (Break down of the fee: Student Services fee: € 72.00 + semester ticket: € 110,10)
You can pay this amount before or after your arrival in Würzburg. It is important that you
transfer the amount before your enrollment
and
submit the proof of payment
at the International Office Incoming (see above).
The semester fee can only be paid by bank transfer. Bank transfer details will be included with your Letter of Acceptance.

Costs and Financing
Costs and Financing
Costs
Semester Contribution
There are no tuition fees at the University of Würzburg. However you must pay the semester contribution each semester for enrollment or re-enrollment. The semester contribution consists of a student contribution and the semester ticket.
More detailed information and the current amount of the semester contribution can be found on the websites of the Registrar’s Office.
Living Costs
The living costs in Würzburg are low compared to other German cities. Of course this also depends strongly on the individual life style, but you should expect monthly costs of about €940.
Eating
250,00 €
Living
350,00 €
Health Insurance
110,00 €
Other
212,00 €
Broadcasting fees (AZDBS/GEZ)*
18,00 €
Total
940,00 €
Further information can be found on the
website of DAAD
.
Broadcasting Fee (GEZ)
If you are staying in Germany longer than three months, you have to pay a broadcasting fee. The registration form can be found
online
.
Monthly fee: 18,36 €
Note
: In a shared flat (WG), the broadcasting fee contribution is a monthly fee for the whole apartment. Talk with your roommates about how you will apportion the fees.
Information and forms
Financing
Scholarships
You can finance your studies or doctoral studies in Germany with the help of scholarships. There are two possibilities to receive a scholarship:
In your home country
: Ask your home university about university partnership scholarships, Erasmus etc. You can also inform yourself about scholarships offered by the Ministry of Education or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
In Germany:
The
database of the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD)
provides an overview of scholarships for foreign students and doctoral candidates. The DAAD also has
offices abroad
where you can get information before departure.
On this website you can find
further information on scholarships
.
Another database for scholarships is
Stipendienlotse
ERASMUS-Mobility-Grant
If you need further information please ask your home University.
Working while you study
If you want to work while you are studying in Germany, please note the following information:
Students from countries within the EU and the EEA
are on equal terms on the labor market and are allowed to work during studies;
Students from other countries
are allowed to work 120 days of full-time work or 240 half days per year (which also concludes voluntary internships). If you would like to work more you need a permission from the agency for employment (Agentur für Arbeit) or the immigration office;
Important: Be sure your studies do not suffer if you have a side job! Please read the information
on the legal framework of the DAAD.
On the following pages you can search for job opportunities in Würzburg:
Federal Employment Agency
(Bundesagentur für Arbeit);
http://www.wuewowas.de/kle/nbj_list.php;
Unterfrankenjobs
;
Career Centre at the University of Wuerzburg;
https://www.jobbörse-stellenangebote.de/stellenangebote-würzburg/
In the pubs, restaurants and cafes in the city of Würzburg;
Student assistant positions at the University of Würzburg
.

Living
Living
WARNING: Please beware of tricksters on the housing market. Do NOT transfer high amounts of deposits beforehand!
Please note:
The University of Würzburg solely provides information for websites and third-party housing offers on the International Office website. The University of Würzburg is not responsible for the content of the respective websites and housing offers. The International Office does not act as an intermediary.
The University assumes no responsibility for the success of finding accommodation. JMU is also not liable for the content of the information provided by the potential tenants as third parties, nor for any possible damages resulting from the use of the information.
Advantage for exchange programme students:
Apply for a room in a dormitory of the Studierendenwerk by the official application deadline (15 June for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester) and your accommodation is guaranteed!
Freemovers
can also apply for a room in a dormitory of The Studierendenwerk, but no room can be guaranteed.
Dormitories of the Student Housing Service (Studierendenwerk)
The
Student Housing Service
is responsible for several dormitories in various locations in Würzburg.
Amenities:
Single and double rooms or rooms in apartments where two to four students share a kitchen and bathroom;
All rooms and apartments are furnished;
Dishes, cooking items, bedding, and towels are not provided;
You can find more information about the individual dormitories on
Studierendenwerk's website
.
Length of stay:
Student accommodations are granted for 6 months (for one semester stay) or 12 months (for one year stay). A shorter rental period is not possible
Participants who participate in the intensive language course
before the semester begins can get a dorm room one month earlier, so that the length of the contract increases to 7 or 13 months
Application:
Deadlines:
June 15 for the Winter Semester and January 15 for the Summer Semester
(Student Housing Service must receive the security deposit by this date);
After your application as an exchange student, you'll will get from us a guide on "How to apply for a room in a dormitory?".
Please apply for a room in a dormitory as soon as you have the guide.
As an exchange student, you do NOT need your letter of acceptance for the dormitory application!
Programme students who apply online by this date are guaranteed to get a dorm room.
Please contact the
Student Housing Service
for any questions regarding your application for a dormitory.
Withdrawal from contract:
Reimbursement of the deposit is only possible within a certain time frame. Please see the Housing Office's website for
further information
.
To increase your chances of getting a room offer, we recommend choosing "single room in any shared apartment" as wished type of housing and for wished student residences "all with single rooms in any shared apartment in Würzburg"

Health Insurance
All students in Germany
MUST
have health insurance.
Students from the European Union or the United Kingdom
Apply for a European Health Insurance Card "EHIC" resp.
Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC)
through your health insurance company.
Please show your EHIC/ GHIC to a German health insurance company. They will confirm that your insurance is adequate for enrolment and send this information electronically to the University of Würzburg.
Important: Enrolment is only possible after the electronic confirmation has been received by the University of Würzburg.
Students from countries that have social security agreement with Germany (e.g. Switzerland, Turkey)
If you are holding statutory health insurance in your home country, your health insurance will also be recognised in Germany.
Please already clarify in your home country which documents are needed for the recognition of health insurance!
Please show these documents to a German health insurance company. They will confirm that your insurance is adequate for enrolment and sned this confirmation to the University of Würzburg electronically.
Important:
Enrolment is only possible after the electronic confirmation has been received by the University of Würzburg.
Students from other countries
Some other health insurances are also valid in Germany. To be valid in Germany, your health insurance must meet the following requirements:
validity for the whole time of stay
entire range of benefits like the German ones
outpatient care
inpatient care
medication
for women: treatment for pregnancy
no limit for the benefits
no waiting period for the benefits
If your health insurance meets all these requirements please show your insurance contract (must be written in German or English) to a German statutory health insurance company so that they can confirm that your insurance is adequate for enrolment.
If your health insurance is not valid in Germany you have to take out a private or statutory health insurance in Germany before or after your arrival:
Statutory health insurance is available for students who do not exceeded 14 semesters of study and are not older than 30 years. The cost (without children) is approximately 110 Euro per month. The cost is the same at all insurance companies.
Private health insurance is usually more expensive and all costs must be paid out of pocket before the insurance company reimburses the costs. Private health insurances must be confirmed by a statutory health insurance company.
Please note:
If you have a private health insurance, you cannot switch to statutory health insurance.
Important:
Enrolment is only possible after we have received the electronic confirmation of your health insurance status from a German statutory health insurance provider.
Further information:
You can find more information about health insurance in Germany on the
Studierendenkanzlei website
, on the
website "studying in Germany"
or on the
DAAD website
.
At some health insurance companies it is possible to insure online. You can find more information about this on the websites of the different health insurance companies.
Liability Insurance
We highly recommend students to have liability insurance while staying in Germany. It can either be bought in Germany or your home insurance covers your exchange period abroad (please check with your provider). Liability insurance covers the responsibility for damage caused to persons, objects or assets up to a certain amount. The higher this amount, the higher the annual fee.

Visa
Visa
Please note:
The University of Wuerzburg is not responsible for the issue of a Visa. Please contact the competent authorities and have a look on the
Consular Services Portal
.
Students with citizenship from an EU or EEA country do
not
need a Visa, just a valid passport
Students from Switzerland do not need a visa to enter Germany. However, if the stay in Germany lasts longer than 3 months, they must register with the responsible immigration authorities.
Students from several other countries (Andorra, Australia, Brazil, Canada, El Salvador, Honduras, Israel, Japan, Monaco, New Zealand, San Marino, South Korea, UK, USA) do
not
need a visa to enter Germany
, but for a
stay in Germany longer than 90 days
, they need a
residence permit
.
If you have already received your notification of admission to university, you should apply for a student visa. Anyone who is still waiting on the notice of admission or who has to sit an entrance examination will need to apply for a student applicant visa.
You can obtain your student visa or your student applicant visa at the
German Embassy or the German Consulate
.
Once you arrive in Germany, you will need to submit your visa to the foreigners' authority in order to convert this to a
residence permit
for study purposes.
Comprehensive information on legal requirements for the entry and residence of international students, academics an scientists can be found in the
leaflet of DAAD
.
Further information in different languages can be found on the
website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
.
To find out whether you need a visa or not, you can also refer to the
list of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Do not enter Germany as a tourist! A tourist visa cannot be converted into a student visa or residence permit!
Request your visa well in advance. Gathering all of the necessary documents can take time.
Important
: Before the expiration of your visa you have to request for a
residence permit
in Germany.
If you are required to have a visa, you must submit a valid visa for enrolment. Without a valid visa, your enrolment cannot be issued.

Resident Permit
Please note
:
EU-Citizen do NOT need a resident permit.
The University of Wuerzburg is
not
responsible for the issue of a resident permit. Please contact the competent authorities.
Students who are not from an EU country need a resident permit.
You can apply for the resident permit right after your arrival and it has to be issued in any case before the expiration of your visa.
Non-EU-Citizen who have not required a visa to enter the country, need nonetheless a residence permit, if they want to stay longer than 90 days in Germany.
The foreigners' Office of your place of residence can issue a residence permit. Make an appointment as soon as possible after your arrival with the
Würzburg Immigration Office
(Ausländeramt) in the City Hall.
If you do not live right in Würzburg town but in Würzburg district, you must contact the
district office
for your resident permit.
You will find further information right

Registration with the City of Würzburg
As soon as you arrive in Würzburg and have received your lease contract / rent agreement, you are required to register your new address in the
City Hall
. You need your passport, your new lease/rent agreement and the
confirmation of accommodation
signed by your lessor at the time of the registration.
For your registration at the Town Hall you need to book an appointment online:
here
.
Important to know: to make sure you get an appointment in time, please make sure you book your appointment aprox. 4 weeks prior to your arrival in Wuerzburg.
Tax-ID
Your tax identification number will be sent to you by post within two weeks of your initial registration with the registration office.
It is possible to request this number directly from the tax office (
Finanzamt
) two days after the initial registration.

First Steps Events
First Steps Events
You have questions concerning your exchange experience at JMU Würzburg (e.g. application, enrolment, housing)? No problem, we got you covered! Come join us and other fellow students for the following first steps events.
Pre-First Steps
The University of Würzburg is waiting to welcome you! To make your transition to our university as smooth as possible, we are offering an online orientation for all incoming students. Be sure to sign up for one of the orientation events listed below – you’ll be glad you did! You’ll have the unique chance to hear directly from our International Students Office Staff and get all of the inside information you need about application, student dorms, getting a visa, German courses, health insurance, and more  – all from the comfort of your own computer.  Don’t miss it!
Our
online
orientation events are available in German or English!
June 10, 2026 at 13:00; Language:  German-low level & English if requiered
June 10, 2026 at 09:00; Language: English
June 10, 2026 at 16:00; Language: English
Be sure to determine what time that corresponds to in your time zone prior to the day of the online event.
Please send an email (
enrolment@uni-wuerzburg.de
) with your preferred time in order to register for the online orientation until June 09,  at 14:00.
First Steps
You have applied and are preparing your exchange semester in Würzburg? Great. You have been with us for a while, but you still have lots of questions? Join us at one of our First Steps Events and learn everything you need to know about accommodation, enrolment, visa, timetable planning, the University’s rules and regulations etc.
Of course, our First Steps Events are also a great way to meet fellow international students! We will offer these events in either
online
or
hybrid mode
(face-to-face and in case you can not join us in person you can join us virtually). Updates can be found on this page, so please stop by every once in a while to be well informed.
When?

Sanderring 2, 97070 and online
16/09/2026  at  18:00,  in German: online

text:
【第1頁】
 
 
Checklist for Exchange Students 
After you have applied to study at the University of Würzburg ( steps to your application) and have 
received your letter of acceptance, there are still a few things you will need to do before beginning 
your studies. The following is a step-by-step list of what you should do: 
 Apply for a student visa (Visum für Studienzwecken) at the German Embassy 
More Information. 
 Accommodation search 
More information. 
 Take out health insurance 
Advice on health insurance. 
 Online Enrolment 
More information. 
 Learning Agreement 
If your home University needs a Learning Agreement, find here useful information. 
 Course selection and schedule 
Students at German universities plan their own course schedule. More information. 
 Getting here 
o By airplane: Airport Frankfurt/Main or Nürnberg with direct ICE-train connections to 
Würzburg https://www.frankfurt-airport.com/en.html, https://www.airport-
nuernberg.de/english. 
o  By train: Easily accessible from all directions: https://www.bahn.com/en/view/index.shtml. 
o Public transport in Würzburg: With the WVV (timetables at https://www.bayern-
fahrplan.de/en/journey-planner?set_language=en) problem-free to the various 
university buildings and student dormitories. 
o By car: There are city maps and site plans on the internet for your orientation in town or 
upon your arrival by car: : https://wueaddress.uni-wuerzburg.de/search/map?q= 
 Dormitory  
o If you have reserved a room at a dormitory with the Studentenwerk Würzburg, you can 
obtain your key from the facilities manager of the respective dormitory Monday to 
Thursday between 7:30 am and 4:00 pm and on Fridays between 7:30 am and 1:00 pm. 
This does not apply on holidays. 
o Please note these holidays when planning your travel! Public holidays in March or April 
(dates vary each year): Good Friday (Karfreitag) and Easter Monday (Ostermontag). 
Check out the holidays in Bavaria. 
o Public holiday on the 3rd of October: Day of German Reunification (Tag der Deutschen 
Einheit).  
 Student ID Card 
To receive the Student ID card, you must first complete the online enrollment. You will also need 
to send some documents to the International Office Incoming by email. More information. 
 Important events after arrival 
You should definitely visit the following events: 
o The orientation event of your faculty. More information. 

【第2頁】
 
 
o The welcome reception and the First Steps orientation events of the International Office 
Incoming. The reception takes place a few days before the start of term. You will be 
informed of the exact time and date as soon as possible. 
o Language level test for courses in German: Please check the dates for the test. 
 Registration of your residence at the registration office 
Further information. 
 Apply for a resident permit (NOT for EU citizen) 
Further information. 
 Enjoy Würzburg and get to know people. 
Here you can find events and activities. 
 
Packing list: 
 
Documents: 
 Passport (non-EU citizens) or ID card (EU citizens) 
 Visa (non-EU citizens) 
 Letter of Acceptance 
 Confirmation of financial means (e.g., scholarship confirmation, only non-EU citizens) 
 If paid in home country: Confirmation of payment of semester fee. 
 Confirmation of health insurance (see above) 
 If available: Vaccination card 
 If you want to drive by car in Germany: International drivers’ licence 
 
Other 
 220 power adapter or a German plug system adapter 
 Clothes for all types of weather. Würzburg enjoys a lot of sun, but can also get cold in winter and 
get rain in spring and fall.

Transcript of Records for Exchange students
Your academic results during your stay at the Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg will be recorded in the Transcript of Records and it will be sent to you.
Upon request, we can also send this document to your home university.
The International Office provides you with your Transcript of Records only upon request.
The process of creating this document depends on your study field.

Frequently Asked Questions
Show all
Hide all
A grade on my transcript is incorrect, please correct it.
​​​​​Please contact the instructor of the course. Only she/he has the authority to make a change to the grade. If the grade changes, we need a notification of this from the lecturer her-/himself (e.g. via e-mail or by issuing a new certificate (”Schein”)).
Can you please confirm my stay at the University of Würzburg (COS)?
Please send us proof of your arrival and departure dates (bus/train ticket, etc.). In addition, please send us the COS template from your home university. We can then confirm your stay.
Can you please merge my transcript from WueStudy with my transcript from you into one?
​​​​​Of course, please send us both documents to this e-mail address:
transcripts@uni-wuerzburg.de
. We will then merge them into one document and issue it. If you also need the original document in addition to the scan, please let us know the postal address.
I am still missing a certificate and cannot reach the lecturer, what can I do?
Please try to contact the lecturer again via e-mail. If you have not received a feedback within 2 weeks, please contact us again. We will see what we can do then.
I have completed the online form but have not yet received my transcript, what do I have to do?
​​​​Please send us the certificates of the courses you have taken, which you have received from the respective lecturers. We can then compare the information and issue your transcript of records.
I have discovered an error on my transcript, can you please correct it?
​​​​​Please tell us where the error lies and the correct data to be entered insteadvia e-mail (
transcripts@uni-wuerzburg.de
). We will then be happy to change the transcript. In order to adjust the grade or ECTS credits awarded, we need the confirmation of the lecturer of the corresponding course.
I have not passed an exam, what now?
​​​​​We can delete the course from your transcript for you or mark it as "failed". Please check with your home university whether they require proof of the failed exam or just the final ECTS score.
I took some courses at the University of Würzburg this semester as an Erasmus student. How do I get my transcript? / I missed the deadline for filling out the online form, what can I do?
Please write an e-mail with your request to
transcripts@uni-wuerzburg.de
. We will send you a template of the document to fill in. In addition, we need the certificates for the courses you have attended. Please also send us all of those so that we can process your request quicker.
What do I enter if I do not know the course number?
​​​​​​Please leave the field blank if you do not know the course number. We will add it later according to the course catalogue.

Exchange students and free movers
Exchange is not a year in life ... it's a life in a year!
The University of Hohenheim is located on the southern outskirts of Stuttgart and is the oldest - and most beautiful - of Stuttgart's universities. Surrounded by botanical gardens and experimental areas, the university offers a unique atmosphere for studying and working. Hohenheim is one of the few campus universities in Germany, which means that all important facilities such as lecture halls, institutes, language center, library, computer rooms, cafeteria, and the Office of International Affairs are within walking distance. The city center itself is about 30 minutes away by public transport.
Come to Hohenheim
Why Hohenheim?
Germany's No. 1 in agricultural research and food sciences, strong and unique in natural, economic, social, and communication sciences, the most beautiful campus in the state, the most popular university in Baden-Württemberg - and nationwide No. 2...
There are many good reasons to come to Hohenheim as an exchange student or free mover!

Exchange students and free movers: Applying
Exchange students and free movers
Application as exchange student or free mover
Hohenheim has long been a university with a strong international orientation and maintains contacts with numerous partner universities. About 12% of the nearly 10,000 students come from abroad - and from more than 100 countries. If you would also like to be part of this group, whether as an exchange student or as a free mover, you will find all the information you need for your application here.
Who can apply
Who can apply to be an exchange student or free mover and what opportunities do you have with this status?
More
Dates
When are the application deadlines? When can you expect to get notification of admission?
More
Application

More
