How to apply as an exchange student
Exchange students are non-degree students who intend to study at the University of Eastern Finland (Joensuu or Kuopio campus) for one or two semesters. These students participate in bilateral or international student exchange programmes (e.g. Erasmus+, FIRST+, ISEP, Nordplus/Nordlys, North2North, bilateral agreements).
In most fields the students are recommended to have the minimum of 2 years of studies in their field before coming for exchange.
Application deadlines
30 April for autumn semester (September - December) or full academic year (September - May) studies
30 September for spring semester (January - May) studies
Please note that
the online application tool SoleMOVE will close at 23.59 (Finnish time) on the given date
, no flexibility here. It is not possible to apply after the deadlines.
In Clinical Medicine
, priority is given to applicants who apply during the first application round in March-April. Applicants who apply in September may be accepted if there are available places after the initial application round. This applies to both studyin and training in Clinical Medicine.
Nominations
The application process starts with a nomination from the partner university to the University of Eastern Finland.  Coordinators at partner universities are asked
to nominate their candidates for student exchange at UEF in the SoleMOVE system
. If your coordinator does not have a SoleMOVE account or have not received instructions on how to activate the account and nominate students, please ask her/him to contact
[email protected]
Once the nomination is approved by the UEF International Mobility Services, the applicants receive usernames for the online application tool SoleMOVE by email. After that, the students can start applying.
The deadline for the nominations
for the autumn semester and for the full academic year is
15 April
and for the spring semester
15 September
.
Nominations done after the deadline will not be considered.
Important! If you have not received an e-mail that contains information on activating your user account, please check your junk mail folder!
How to nominate your students:
Coordinators at partner universities are asked to nominate their candidates for student exchange at UEF
in the SoleMOVE system
. If you do not have a SoleMOVE account or have not received instructions on how to activate the account and nominate students, please contact
[email protected]
Note that nomination done after the deadline will not be considered.
Activating the SoleMOVE user account
When you have received the e-mail containing your SoleMOVE username, click the activation link. You can choose your own password. Enter it twice and activate the account. Then you can log in. Do not delete the activation e-mail – it contains your username and the link to the application system. You will need them later. Please note that the system works best with Internet Explorer and Mozilla Firefox. Safari is not recommended. You should use the login option 'Local', NOT 'Shibboleth'.
User instructions
You will have access to the complete user manual you have logged in. You will find it in the upper left corner by clicking the question mark.
Application check list
1) Application form – Compulsory
Complete the form in the online application tool. Check the information that is already there, and be careful to spell your name as it appears in your passport. Capitalise the first letter, leave the rest lower case.
2) Official Transcript of Academic Records – Compulsory
A Transcript of Academic Records is your complete academic record with the information on completed courses, grades and credits.
An English translation of the Transcript of Academic Records is required.
Application cannot be processed without the transcript because the academic departments of the University of Eastern Finland need to check the applicant's academic background and suitability for the intended studies.
Scan your transcript and upload it as an attachment to your application.
If you have completed a Bachelor's degree earlier, please make sure you attach also the transcript of the Bachelor's studies with your application.
3) Learning agreement – Compulsory
Use the form your home university gives you. Complete the learning agreement clearly with BLOCK letters or type electronically.
The learning agreement must be signed by the applicant and by the home coordinator.
Please note that your learning agreement will be only provisionally accepted, and you may need to revise it once you arrive in Finland.
Scan the signed learning agreement and upload it as an attachment to your application. If your home university does not have a form for the Learning Agreement, please use the UEF one at
Forms for incoming exchange students - UEF Kamu
- > Learning Agreement (incoming non-Erasmus students). Also note that having your Learning Agreement approved does not mean that you have secured a place on those courses – you need to register for them when you have arrived.
Information on the courses for exchange students in Peppi:
Courses for exchange students | Opinto-opas 2026-2027
4) Copy of an ID - Compusory
Scan a copy of your ID (for example a passport or another ID with a photo).
5) Other information
Language tests are NOT required from the students coming from our partner universities.
Motivation Letter is optional.
Letters of reference are optional.
In order to avoid any delays in the application process, please make sure that you have carefully filled in all sections of the application form, enclosed required documents and collected all necessary signatures.
Submitting the application
You do not have to complete the whole application at once – if you do not have all the information ready, you can save your progress and continue later. Be sure that you have filled in all the necessary information and attached all enclosures before you send your application. It is not possible for you to change anything in your application after you have submitted it.
Submitting the application in SoleMOVE is enough. You do not need to send us a printed copy.
Admission procedure
The faculties of the University of Eastern Finland admit the students. After receiving your application, the International Mobility Services will forward it to appropriate academic department. The department then processes the application and the proposed learning agreement. Once the International Mobility Services receive an official confirmation of acceptance from the faculty/department, an official admission document is issued and sent to you by e-mail 1-2 months after the application period has ended. Please do not make any definite travel plans or reserve accommodation before you have received the official acceptance.
Help and further information
If you have technical problems with the application tool, send an e-mail to:
[email protected]
.
If you have any questions or concerns, please contact the International Mobility Services:
[email protected]
.
How to apply as a visiting student
Visiting students are international non-degree students who intend to study at the University of Eastern Finland (Joensuu or Kuopio Campus) for one or two semesters. These students do not participate in bilateral or international student exchange programmes (e.g. Erasmus, FIRST, bilateral agreement).
Students are entitled to official student status (e.g. student cards) at the university. Since visiting students are non-degree students, official diplomas or certificates, other than transcripts, are not available after the study period. Please note that studies for visiting students cannot be guaranteed in all departments of the University of Eastern Finland.
Requirements
Applicants must be registered at their home university and also be recommended for admission by the home university (see below: Nominations). Applicants must have studied for at least one academic year at a university in a related study field. Applicants must have good command of spoken and written English. Applicants can support the application by including a voluntary language test certificate.
Financing of the studies
The tuition fee for visiting students is 3500 euros for the full academic year or 1750 euros for one semester. Tuition fee is also required if exchange lasts less than one semester (e.g. if visiting student stays at the University of Eastern Finland for three months, his/her tuition fee is 1750 euros). Visiting students cannot register before the tuition fee is paid, and the proof of the payment is required to provide on arrival.
Finnish authorities also require non-EU applicants to prove that they have adequate funds for living expenses (800 euros/ month for duration of stay in Finland) when applying for a student's residence permit. Please note that the University of Eastern Finland does not offer scholarships or other financial support for visiting students.
Application deadlines
30 April for Autumn Semester (September – December) or Full Academic Year (September – May)
30 September for Spring Semester (January – May)
Please, note that it is not possible to apply after the deadlines.
Nominations
The application process begins when the University of Eastern Finland receives nomination e-mails from universities abroad. In other words, study abroad coordinators send an e-mail to the International Mobility Services in which they announce their candidates for student exchange. After that, International Mobility Services sends applicants usernames for the online application tool SoleMOVE by e-mail to the student.
Nominations should include:
1. Student's complete name
2. Date of birth
3. Gender
4. E-mail address
5. Duration of exchange (autumn semester, spring semester or full academic year)
6. Studies/internship
The deadline for autumn semester and full academic year nominations is 15 April and for the spring semester 15 September.
Important! If you have not received an e-mail that contains information on activating your user account, check your junk mail folder!
Activating the SoleMOVE user account
When you have received the e-mail containing your SoleMOVE username, click the activation link. You can choose your own password. Enter it twice and activate the account. Then you can log in. Do not delete the activation e-mail – it contains your username and the link to the application system. You will need them later.
User instructions
You will have access to the complete user manual when you have logged in. You will find it in the upper left corner by clicking the question mark.
Check list for the application
A) Application form – Compulsory
Complete the form in the online application tool. Check the information that is already there, and be careful to spell your name as it appears in your passport. Capitalise the first letter, leave the rest lower case.
B) Enclosures
1. Official Transcript of Academic Records – Compulsory
A Transcript of Academic Records is your complete academic record with the information on completed courses, grades and credits.
An English translation of the Transcript of Academic Records is required.
Application cannot be processed without the transcript because the academic departments of the University of Eastern Finland need to check the applicant's academic background and suitability for the intended studies.
Scan your transcript and upload it as an attachment to your application.
2. Learning Agreement – Compulsory
Use the form your home university gives you. Complete the Learning agreement clearly with BLOCK letters or type electronically.
The Learning agreement must be signed by the applicant, the departmental coordinator and the institutional coordinator (if available).
Scan the signed Learning agreement and upload it as an attachment to your application. If your home university does not have a form for the Learning Agreement, please use the UEF one at
Forms for incoming exchange students - UEF Kamu
- > Learning Agreement (incoming non-Erasmus students). Also note that having your Learning Agreement approved does not mean that you have secured a place on those courses – you need to register for them when you have arrived.
Information on the courses in Peppi:
Courses for exchange students | Opinto-opas 2026-2027
3. A scanned copy of an official ID – Compulsory
Scan the identification page of your passport or other official ID as an attachment to your application.
4. Two Letters of Reference
One of the two needs to be from your Academic Advisor
Scan the letters and upload them as an attachment to your application. Please scan them both as one file.
5. Motivation letter
Describes your motivation to study at the University of Eastern Finland
Includes study and financial plan
Scan and upload as an attachment to your application.
Other information
In order to avoid any delays in the application process, please make sure that you have carefully filled in all sections of the application form, enclosed required documents and collected all necessary signatures.
Please note that incomplete applications will not be considered.
Submitting the application
You do not have to complete the whole application at once – if you do not have all the information ready, you can save your progress and continue later. Be sure that you have filled in all the necessary information and attached all enclosures before you send your application. It is not possible for you to change anything in your application after you have submitted it.
Submitting the application in SoleMOVE is enough. You do not need to send us a printed copy.
Admission procedure
The faculties of the University of Eastern Finland admit the students. After receiving your application, the International Mobility Services will forward it to appropriate academic department. The department then processes the application and the proposed study plan. Once the International Mobility Services receive an official confirmation of acceptance from the faculty/department, an official admission document is issued and sent to you 1-2 months after the application period has ended. Please do not make any definite travel plans or reserve accommodation before you have received the official acceptance.
Help and further information
If you have technical problems with the application tool, send an e-mail to:
[email protected]
.
If you have any questions or concerns, please contact the International Mobility Services:
[email protected]
.
Erasmus training and Freemover training
Erasmus training or Freemover training is suitable for non-degree exchange students who intend to do training (e.g. clinical placement, research work) in one of the departments of the University of Eastern Finland. The duration of Erasmus Training or Freemover Training is either one or two semesters (or in some cases a shorter period), but always a minimum of two months. Please note that there is a limited number of training options at the University of Eastern Finland, and departments are not obligated to organise training for the applicants.
Before applying as a trainee, the students have to negotiate the training directly with the department they are interested in.  However, the students in Clinical Medicine should not contact the Medical Clinics/Departments at the University Hospital directly but the teaching coordinator in Clinical Medicine.
Please also note that Erasmus trainees are not allowed to do regular courses at the University of Eastern Finland.
Recommended application deadlines for training applicants
30 April for Autumn Semester (September - December) or full academic year (September - May)
30 September for Spring Semester (January - May)
In Clinical Medicine
, priority is given to applicants who apply during the first application round in March-April. Applicants who apply in September may be accepted if there are available places after the initial application round. This applies to both studyin and training in Clinical Medicine.
Nominations
The application process starts with
a nomination from the partner university to the University of Eastern Finland
.  Coordinators at partner universities are asked to nominate their candidates for student exchange at UEF in SoleMOVE system. If your coordinator does not have a SoleMOVE account or have not received instructions on how to activate the account and nominate students, please ask her/him to contact
[email protected]
Once the nomination is approved by the UEF International Mobility Services, the applicants receive usernames for the online application tool SoleMOVE by email. After that the students can start applying.
Important! If you have not received an e-mail that contains information on activating your user account, check your junk mail folder!
The recommended deadline
for the nominations for the autumn semester and for the full academic year is 15 April and for the spring semester 15 September.
How to nominate your students:
Coordinators at partner universities are asked to nominate their candidates for student exchange at UEF in SoleMOVE system. If you do not have a SoleMOVE account or have not received instructions on how to activate the account and nominate students, please contact
[email protected]
Activating the SoleMOVE user account
When you have received the e-mail containing your SoleMOVE username, click the activation link. You can choose your own password. Enter it twice and activate the account. Then you can log in. Do not delete the activation e-mail – it contains your username and the link to the application system. You will need them later.
User instructions
You will have access to the complete user manual when you have logged in. You will find it in the upper left corner by clicking the question mark.
Application check list
1) Application form – Compulsory
Be sure to choose ‘P – Traineeship' as the type of exchange. Check the information that is already there, and be careful to spell your name as it appears in your passport. Capitalise the first letter, leave the rest lower case.
2) Official Transcript of Academic Records – Compulsory
A Transcript of Academic Records is your complete academic record with the information on completed courses, grades and credits.
An English translation of the Transcript of Academic Records is required.
Application cannot be processed without the transcript because the academic departments of the University of Eastern Finland need to check the applicant's academic background and suitability for the intended training.
Scan your transcript and upload it as an attachment to your application.
3) Placement agreement/Learning agreement for traineeships – Compulsory
Use the form your university gives you. Complete the form clearly with BLOCK letters or type electronically.
If you intend to work in a research project, please indicate the name of your supervisor and type of the project.
The agreement must be signed by the applicant and by the sending institution. When the student is accepted, the agreement will be signed by UEF department.
Scan the signed agreement (signatures from the applicant and from the sending institution) and upload it as an attachment to your application.
4) Curriculum Vitae (CV) – Compulsory
Upload your CV as an attachment to your application.
5) Copy of an ID - Compulsory
Scan a copy of your ID (for example a passport or another ID with a photo).
6) Other
Letters of reference are optional.

The independent nature of UAS studies in Finland presupposes that students show initiative 
and take responsibility for the planning of their studies and for keeping to their own schedules. 
LAB being a university of applied sciences also means that the approach is very practical, 
including less theory and more projects. The study methods at LAB support self-guided 
development, which creates a basis for comprehensive learning: lectures, teamwork, projects, 
reading assignments and essays.  
In addition to face-to-face lectures, LAB also offers many online courses in Moodle learning 
platform. 
 
Please note that there is no specific exam period at the end of the term; exams are held 
throughout the academic year. 
 
English language requirement minimum level is B2.

Grading system Finnish higher education institutions use numeric grading scales. At L AB, the scale is from 5 
(excellent) to 1 (sufficient). Every course and examination at L AB is recorded on the student’s 
personal transcript. Below is a comparison table with other ECTS grading scale.  
 
LAB grading scale European grade definition (not official equivalents) 
5 Excellent  A 
4 Very good      B 
3 Good              C 
2 Satisfactory   D 
1 Sufficient       E  
0 Fail  
 
Please note that some courses are without grading on a pass/fail basis. In this case the mark 
‘pass’ appears on the transcript.  
Credit system 
Work load / year 
 
Finnish higher education institutions use ECTS credit system. The estimated workload for full 
time student in one academic year is 60 ECTS credits, meaning 30 ECTS credits per semester.  
Please note that a credit does not refer to the duration of a course, but to the estimated 
amount of work required. One credit refers to approximately 27 hours of work by the student. 
Credits are used to define the extent of a given course. Lectures, projects, assignments and 
other forms of studies are all taken into consideration when the number of credits for each 
course is calculated. 
Finnish language 
courses 
LAB offers courses in intercultural communication and interdisciplinary courses in our focus 
areas of design, environmental engineering and welfare as well as courses about Finnish 
language and culture.

persons. 
More information at https://lahdentalot.fi/exchangestudents/?lang=en

Lappeenranta 
In Lappeenranta students can apply for student accommodation in the Lappeenranta Student 
Housing Foundation LOAS at www.loas.fi/en   
Please apply for the accommodation directly from LOAS and by the given date. Students might 
need to apply for housing even if they have not yet received the acceptance letter from LAB 

【第5頁】

 Updated February 21, 2023 
  
  
University of Applied Sciences. LOAS will send only one housing offer per applicant. If a student 
rejects the offer, it might be very difficult to find another accommodation .

Visas and permits  1. Citizens of the Nordic countries need not apply for a residence permit but have to register 
at a Digital and Population Data Services Agency if they stay in Finland longer than six 
months. Please see also  HalloNorden! -Information pages for possible practices of your 
home country. 
2.  Citizens of other EEA countries need to register their right of residence in Finland if they 
plan to stay in Finland for more than 3 months non-stop. They can do the registration at the 
Finnish Immigration Service within 90 days of their arrival to Finland. Please see information 
on http://www.migri.fi/eu_registration.    
3. Persons from outside the Nordic and the EEA countries who intend to stay in Finland for 
more than 3 months need a residence permit which should be acquired before arrival in 
Finland at the nearest Finnish embassy or consulate. Please see the Finnish Immigration 
Flowchart: Residence Permit for Studies at www.migri.fi.   
4. Each student needs to do registration into Population Information System in Finland. This is 
advised and done during the Orientation Programme.   
 
LAB only provides the above information as general guidance regarding residence permits and 
visa issues and is in no way responsible for official rules and regulations regarding their 
distribution. As immigration policy is subject to change, all international  applicants should 
consult the Finnish Immigration Service for up-to-date information regarding residence permits. 
 
More information at online exchange student guide. All international students need to apply 
Finnish Personal Identity Code. Student entering Finland with residence permit can apply Finnish 
PIC within the residence permit application. Finnish PIC can be applied from Digital and 
Population Data Services Agency once arrival. Instructions are given within the Orientation 
Programme.

Article
Student housing in LAB's campus cities
Created
11.12.2025
How do university students arrange their accommodation in Finland? What are the accommodation options for students?
Finland does not have a dormitory system on campuses, but there are housing providers for affordable, effortless, and safe student accommodation in both LAB's campus cities, Lahti and Lappeenranta. Applying for an apartment is the student’s responsibility.
In Finland, higher education students commonly live in studio or one-bedroom apartments or in shared apartments with other students. In most shared apartments, students have their own bedrooms and share other living spaces with their roommates.
In many cases, the rent for student apartments includes internet access and heating. In many student apartment buildings, you have access to a common laundry room and sauna. Student accommodation is usually located either near the campus or with convenient public transport access to the campus.
The winter might be cold, but the apartments are warm
Houses and apartments in Finland are high-quality, well-insulated, and double-glazed as a default. They are designed to keep warm air inside and are therefore well-heated during winters.
So, even if the cold winter weather can feel uninviting or even harsh at times, you can escape it inside your warm apartment. Finnish people also have a few tricks up their sleeves to keep warm during winter: coffee, sauna, and layered clothing.
Student apartments in Lahti
Lahden Talot
is a housing company owned by the City of Lahti and the main provider of student housing in the region. Living in Lahti is affordable, and student apartments are available around the city. Both students and graduates can easily find suitable rental apartments.
Average rent prices per month for students in Lahti
Rooms in shared apartments €350–€450
Studio apartments €500
One-bedroom apartments €600
Family apartments €750
Student apartments in Lappeenranta
LOAS
provides housing for all students in Lappeenranta. Their apartments are high-quality, well-maintained, and affordable. Most are located near the campus, but some are also available in the city centre.
Average rent prices per month for students in Lappeenranta
Rooms in shared apartments €280–€370
Studio apartments €410
One-bedroom apartments €570
Family apartments €720

Arrival to Finland and practical matters- incoming exchange students
After you have been accepted to study at LAB University of Applied Sciences, it's time to start planning your trip to Finland!
In this webpage we have collected some important information what exchange student is good to know.
How to get to Lahti and Lappeenranta
The city of Lahti is about 100 km from Helsinki.
Arriving at Lahti campus.
The city of Lappeenranta is located in South Karelia, some 220 km northeast of Finland’s capital, Helsinki.
Arriving to Lappeenranta campus,
By train:
Direct Express or Intercity trains from Helsinki to Lahti take one hour, and to Lappeenranta two hours. You can take a train also from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport.
vr.fi/en
By bus:
Express coaches from Helsinki:
expressbus.fi/en
Low-cost bus connections:
onnibus.com/home
By car:
Take motorway number 4 from Helsinki to Lahti (100 km) and highway number 12 from Lahti via Kouvola to Lappeenranta.
Campus cities and accommodation
Lahti
Lahti City and Campus
Lahti is situated in the southern part of Finland and it is part of the Helsinki metropolitan area. Its location makes it easy to travel to the biggest cities in Finland and to the neighboring countries. As a city it is known for its environmental expertise and for being a renowned design center. Lahti hosts a great variety of activities throughout the year, from cultural to world class sporting events.
Lahti campus
The new Lahti campus is a modern learning environment which is built on former factory premises. Mixing old and new provides a unique and inspiring setting for learning and working. More information
here
.
Accommodation in Lahti
Every exchange student is responsible for applying for and finding their own accommodation.
In Lahti students can apply for student accommodation at the Kuukkeli-Kodit and Lahden Talot.
Please apply for the accommodation as soon as you receive the acceptance letter from LAB.
Note!
Please do not make your housing application before you have received an official acceptance for exchange period by LAB.
Kuukkeli-Kodit
Kuukkeli-Kodit offers furnished flats. All of them are shared room apartments. Please note that Kuukkeli-Kodit will make you only one housing offer. It is highly recommended to accept that offer, if you wish to have an apartment by the time your studies begin. The application for housing is made in Kuukkeli-Kodit website. More information
here
.
All questions related to the accommodation at Kuukkeli-Kodit must be addressed to
kuukkeli@kuukkeli-kodit.fi
Lahden Talot
Lahden Talot
offers furnished and unfurnished flats. Most of the exchange students will be located in shared apartments, but couples and families may also get a place in a studio or two-room apartment. Mention in your application that you are an exchange student.
Please note that Lahden Talot will make you only one housing offer. It is highly recommended to accept that offer, if you wish to have an apartment by the time your studies begin. The application for housing is made in Lahden Talot website (follow the link from the bottom of this page). If you do not get a furnished apartment, please contact your tutor (after you have been appointed one) to get tips where to find cheap furniture.
All questions related to the accommodation at Lahden Talot must be addressed to
asiakaspalvelu@lahdentalot.fi
Other housing service providers
Flatta
is a housing marketplace designed for exchange students and summer faculty. Whether you're heading abroad and want to sublet your apartment, or arriving in Finland and need a furnished place for your semester - Flatta connects you safely and handles everything digitally. Already used by hundreds of students across Finland.
You can check other housing service providers from our
housing
website.
Lappeenranta
Lappeenranta City and Campus
Lappeenranta’s special location in the border region between the East and the West, on the southern shore of the fourth largest lake in Europe, Saimaa, has favored and shaped local business and industry and also added unique features to the local culture. Throughout history, excellent transport links in all directions have been considered to be a vital element for the vitality of the region. The region’s natural beauty and Karelian atmosphere attract visitors to the area.
Lappeenranta Campus
Lappeenranta campus, shared by LAB University of Applied Sciences and LUT University, is the largest higher education campus in Southeast Finland. 10 000 people work there, 3 400 of them being LAB students.
More information
here
.
Accommodation in Lappeenranta
Every exchange student is responsible for applying for and finding their own accommodation.
LOAS
In Lappeenranta students can apply for student accommodation at the Lappeenranta Student Housing Foundation LOAS. More information
here
.
All questions related to the accommodation must be addressed to LOAS,
info@loas.fi
(general address)
Note!
Please do not make your housing application before you have received an official acceptance for exchange period by LAB.
We recommend our exchange students to also apply for shared accommodation and we recommend that you select as many different apartments as possible for your application.
Other housing service providers
Flatta
is a housing marketplace designed for exchange students and summer faculty. Whether you're heading abroad and want to sublet your apartment, or arriving in Finland and need a furnished place for your semester - Flatta connects you safely and handles everything digitally. Already used by hundreds of students across Finland.
If you don´t get a housing offer from LOAS or you want to check other housing service providers please see our
housing
website.
Student services, benefits and everyday essentials
LAB Student Account
You will receive a personal username and an official student email account upon your arrival. You will have access to Microsoft's cloud service Office 365.
Personal computer/mobile device – BYOD
Courses at LAB University of Applied Sciences are delivered flexibly, utilizing digital solutions. Various electronic platforms and materials are used in the learning process and course contents. Students connect to the learning environment using their own mobile devices, such as a laptop or a tablet with a keyboard. LAB provides a wireless network on campus as well as support for using your own device.
Tutor Students
All exchange students will get their own personal tutor student. The tutor student will be in contact with you before your arrival to Finland, meet you on your arrival in the Travel Centre and show you around LAB and the city. Tutor students will also help and support you during your whole exchange period in Finland.
The tutor students are second year or older degree students at LAB. You can ask the tutors anything, the answer is not always known, but at least they know where to get help. Besides helping you, the tutors will also take care that you enjoy your student life by arranging different kinds of events during the academic year.
Remember though, that the best thing about being in a foreign country is to find things out by your own and to notice that you really are able to survive in new surroundings, although it may not always be easy. This gives you the best memories and experiences.
Academic Library
Lahti
You can get yourself a personal library card from the academic library of LAB University of Applied Sciences. The library card is available for free and applied online. In Lahti the library is located at the campus (Mukkulankatu 19).
Lappeenranta
LUT Academic Library provides library services in different specialist fields for researchers and the general public. It is one of the European Documentation Centres in Finland and the joint library for the LUT University and LAB University of Applied Sciences. The library has an extensive collection of literature titles and journals, both in print and electronic format.
Accessibility
We provide individual support for exchange students with special needs. Our student exchange coordinators make the required arrangements together with the student service experts. Please be in contact well in advance if individual support is needed.
Student Meals
As an exchange student at LAB you will get a student price meal in our campus restaurants​. The price per lunch is 2.95 €. You will receive the KELA meal subsidy card during the orientation, which entitles you to the discounted price.
Sport Activities
MOVEO provides high quality, affordable and versatile sports services for higher education students. MOVEO members get an access to gym and group exercise lessons.
MOVEO Lahti
MOVEO Lappeenranta
Student Union and Student Card
The student union of LAB University of Applied Sciences is
KOE
. KOE's mission is to make sure that your studies go as smoothly as possible. They promote the interests of all the students of LAB and the quality of education. They make the students’ voice heard in the decisions that concern students. KOE also organizes events and free time activities to counterbalance the busy student life.
As a member of the student union you will get a student card. With the student card, you are entitled to a huge amount of member benefits and discounts in Finland. As a member of KOE you also get benefits at KOE’s events.
ESN - Erasmus Student Network
Hello new student, and congratulations on your study spot!
We are your friendly local section of Erasmus Student Network, or ESN. You can find one of our sections in both Lappeenranta and Lahti! The sections are independent and exist for students, by students. Each section's mission is to bridge the gap between international and domestic community here in Finland. Sections mainly focus their events towards exchange students, however anyone who is internationally minded can and should be apart of the community! All of the events are held in English, and ESN also works with partners around Finland to offer you unforgettable trips to places like the Finnish Lapland!
We hope to see you soon!
Best,
ESN Lappeenranta
and
ESN Lahti
Public transport in Lahti
The student discount for a season ticket is 30% of the price of an adult season ticket. The discounts are valid for the entire LSL (Local and regional bus transport in Lahti) service area. There is no student discount for single and mobile tickets.
More information about LSL student discount
here
.
More information about purchasing the Waltti travel card from
here
. Make sure you have your ID and the necessary certificates with you.
Public transport in Lappeenranta
Full-time students can get a student discount on personal season and value tickets in Lappeenranta public transport, regardless of their municipality of residence. Student status must be updated at the customer service point at the beginning of the academic year or semester. A valid student card or student certificate is sufficient proof of student status.
More information about tickets and prices
Emergency services
In case of emergency, call 112. This number connects you to the ambulance service, police, and fire department. The service workers speak Finnish, Swedish, and English well. Emergency services are trusted in Finland, and your situation will be handled professionally and with care.
It is a good idea to install the free
112 Suomi application
on your phone. When making an emergency call through the app, your exact location (even if you are in a moving car) will automatically be shared with the emergency response centre.

Exams
Grading
Finnish higher education institutions use numeric grading scales. 
At LAB, the scale is from 5 (excellent) to 1 (sufficient). Every course 
and examination at LAB is recorded in the student’s personal 
transcript. Below is a comparison table with other ECTS grading 
scale. 
ECTS
Finnish higher education institutions use ECTS credit system. The esti-
mated workload for a full time student in one academic year is 60 
ECTS credits, meaning 30 ECTS credits per semester.
Please note that a credit does not refer to the duration of a course, 
but to the estimated amount of work required. 
One credit refers to approximately 27 hours of work by the student. 
Credits are used to define the extent of a given course. Lectures, proj-
ects, assignments and other forms of studies are all taken into consider-
ation when the number of credits for each course is calculated.

Visas and permits
Citizens of the Nordic countries need not apply for a residence permit but have to regis-
ter at a Digital and Population Data Services Agency if they stay in Finland longer than six 
months. 
Citizens of other EEA countries need to register their right of residence in Finland if they 
plan to stay in Finland for more than 3 months non-stop. They can do the registration at 
the Finnish Immigration Service within 90 days of their arrival to Finland. Please see infor-
mation on http://www.migri.fi/eu_registrationP
ersons from outside the Nordic and the EEA countries who intend to stay in Finland 
for more than 3 months need a residence permit which should be acquired before arrival 
in Finland at the nearest Finnish embassy or consulate. Please see the Finnish Immigra-
tion Flowchart: Residence Permit for Studies at www.migri.fi.
All international students need to apply Finnish Personal Identity Code (PIC) and this 
way registrate into the Finnish Population Information System. Student s entering Fin-
land with a residence permit can apply Finnish PIC within the residence permit applica-
tion. Finnish PIC can be applied from Digital and Population Data Services Agency once 
arrival. Instructions are given within the Orientation Programme.1.

should consult the Finnish Immigration Service for up-to-date information regarding resi-
dence permits.
More information can be found at online exchange student guide.
LAB provides courses in intercultural 
communication and interdisciplinary studies 
across our key fields of design, environmental 
engineering, and welfare. We also offer courses in 
Finnish language and culture
Finnish Personal Identity Code (PIC)

【第7頁】
All students are responsible for their own insurance arrangements 
and we strongly recommend taking a comprehensive insurance for 
the stay in Finland. Health insurance is a requirement for obtaining a 
residence permit for studies in Finland.

essibility and individual study arrangements
LAB University of Applied Sciences is committed to providing equal 
educational opportunity for students and staff with disabilities. 
Practical procedures will be discussed case by case. Please be in 
touch as soon as possible for practical arrangements.

How to apply to an exchange at LAB?
Breadcrumb

Incoming Exchange Student Guide
How to apply to an exchange at LAB?
Conditions for student exchange
If you are interested in a student exchange period at LAB University of Applied Sciences, please contact your home institution's international office. You can be considered as an exchange student if there is a student exchange agreement between your home institution and LAB University of Applied Sciences. The home institution selects the candidates for student exchange. After you have been selected by your home institution to be a candidate for student exchange and your home institution has nominated you, you can apply to LAB as an exchange student.
Freemover exchange
If your home institution does not have an exchange agreement with LAB University of Applied Sciences, you can come to LAB as a freemover exchange student. In this case a nomination is not required.
The freemover exchange students are subject to a fee.
The fee for the 2026/2027 academic year is
5 500
euros per semester
. Please note that the fee is reviewed annually and may be subject to change. The instructions on how to pay the fee are sent to accepted freemover exchange students along with the acceptance letter.
If you want to apply as a freemover exchange student, please fill out the Application form below. After submitting the form, you will receive an email with instructions on how to register to LAB Mobility-Online. After registering, you can log in to LAB Mobility-Online and upload the required attachments to your application. More information about application deadlines and required documents can be found further down on this page.
Note. The application form will be opened around a month before the application deadlines.
Next application period will be 15.9.–15.10.2026.
Application form for freemover exchange students
Application timeline and process
Nomination Deadlines
Autumn Semester/Academic year: 23rd of April
Spring Semester: 8th of October
Application Deadlines
Autumn semester/Academic year: 30th of April
Spring semester: 15th of October
Application Procedure
All exchange students apply to LAB University of Applied Sciences on the online application system, and all correspondence will be conducted via email. Please note that a valid and operational email address is essential for your application.
Please read through the application instructions step by step before starting the online application.
Application Documents
After your home institution has nominated you, you will get an email invitation to register to our Mobility-Online system and fill in your application. After completing your application, upload the following documents to your account in LAB Mobility-Online:
1. A recent picture of yourself
A photo of yourself (max. 500 pixel x 500 pixel)
2. Copy of your passport/EU ID card
Clear photo of the ID page of your passport, or a photo of your European ID card, if you are an EU citizen.
3. A certificate of competence in English level B2
You are expected to have sufficient skills in English language to be able to study at LAB. If English is not your native language, a document proving your knowledge of English is required. The expect English level is B2 (CEFR level). NOTE! The students whose native is English, can attach a free-form document stating that the student's mother tongue is English.
Approved language tests and specific requirements:
A certificate/document from your home institution (e.g. a teacher, language center or the International Office) in English stating that you have B2 level competence of English.
IELTS Academic, IELTS indicator or IELTS Online
Minimum overall score 6.5, all band scores at least 5.5
PTE Academic or PTE Academic Online
Minimum overall score 62, all band scores at least 54
TOEFL iBT and TOEFL iBT Home Edition
Minimum overall score 90, writing score min. 22
TOEFL iBT (new version in 2026)
Minimum score 4,5
Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency
Minimum Score level C
Cambridge B2 First
Minimum score 170
Cambridge International IGCSE
First language in English Syllabus 0500 and 0990
SAT test Evidence-Based Reading and Writing
Minimum score 600
Oxford ELLT
Minimum score 7
A Degree completed in English
Proof of completing an upper secondary degree or at least Bachelor/Master degree in English at an institution located in the following countries: an EU or EEA country, Australia, South Africa, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, or the United States. The official document must state that English was the language of instructions; if the language is not specified or multiple languages are listed, at least half of the credits must have been completed in English.
4. Transcript of Records in English
Transcript of Records in English (certificate of the courses you have completed in the home institution)
5. Learning Agreement (Study Plan)
Learning Agreement (study plan) according to the instructions on LAB Mobility-Online (
available courses will be listed here
)
Please choose the courses for your Learning Agreement from the list of your study field (can be found from "Studies" section). Note that exchange students are expected to complete 30 ECTS credits during the semester.
Erasmus+ students: Erasmus+ students' Learning Agreements are processed in Erasmus without papers network as data transfer. Erasmus+ students should therefore create the Learning Agreement according to the instructions from their home institution in the system the home institution is using.
Non-Erasmus student: Non-Erasmus students should create a Learning Agreement in LAB Mobility-Online according to the instructions available on the platform.
6. Portfolio - only for students applying to Institute of Design and Fine Arts
Institute of Design and Fine Arts requires a portfolio as an application document. Please read through the additional portfolio instructions before preparing your portfolio:
Think how to stand out from the crowd by presenting your best work in the best light. Be brave and unique. You should also add a motivation letter in your portfolio (max. 1 page). Tell about yourself briefly. Why do you want to study Design? What can you do? Why are you applying to this Department? What are your plans after studying? Tell briefly about your previous education and work experience or hobbies, how they have helped you to learn?
Please send a digital portfolio. Upload your portfolio as PDF-file to your application documents in Mobility Online. Size max. 5MB. Name your file: Lastname_Firstname_portfolio_Departmentname.pdf

After acceptance - incoming exchange students
To be accepted for an exchange at LAB, you need to submit an application in our LAB Mobility-Online system. Once you have submitted your application and all the required documents to LAB, and we have accepted your application, you will receive an acceptance letter via email. Please read the acceptance letter carefully and follow the instructions given.
Welcome to LAB University of Applied Sciences - we want you to have a great experience studying with us!
Important points
Accept the study place
We instruct our exchange students in their acceptance letters on how to accept a study place.
Accommodation
Every exchange student is responsible for applying for and finding their own accommodation. You should start applying for housing as soon as you get your acceptance letter.
Note
that housing companies usually will make you only one housing offer so it is highly recommended to accept that offer, if you wish to have an apartment by the time your studies begin.
Make sure you are applying housing in the correct study city. (Campus information is mentioned in the your application and letter of acceptance)
On the
Arrival to Finland and practical matters- incoming exchange students | eLAB
p
age, you can find different housing companies that operate in Lahti and Lappeenranta.
Check List
LAB has made a Check List for new students. That Check List reminds you of the most important things to do. Here you can find that
Check List
.
Learning agreement
After your acceptance your departmental coordinator can sign your learning agreement. Also if there are any changes needed to do in your Learning agreement, then contact your departmental coordinator/tutor teacher. You can find this information in your LAB Mobility-Online application and also in your acceptance letter.
Living in Finland
Welcome to the land of a thousand lakes, where pristine nature meets cutting-edge innovation – welcome to Finland. Whether you're enchanted by the allure of the northern lights, intrigued by the rhythm of the midnight sun, or captivated by the warmth of Finnish hospitality, living in Finland offers an unparalleled experience. Join us as we delve into the essence of life in Finland, where tradition meets modernity, and every moment is filled with wonder. Welcome to your Finnish adventure.
Tervetuloa Suomeen! (Welcome to Finland in Finnish)
I recommend you take a look at our Living in Finland website.
Here we have collected most impostant information about Finland.
Residence permit
Citizens of the Nordic countries
Citizens of the Nordic countries need not to apply for a residence permit.
Kindly note that all exchange students have to register at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency. Please find the instructions and timetable for the registration from
Student's cheklist
item number 14.
If you are staying more than 90 days uninterrupted in Finland, you also need to register EU citizen's right of residence. Read more
here
.
Citizens of other EEA countries
Citizens of other EEA countries need to register their right of residence in Finland if they plan to stay in Finland for more than 3 months non-stop. They can do the registration at the Finnish Immigration Service within 90 days of their arrival to Finland. Please see information on
http://www.migri.fi/eu_registration
Kindly note that all exchange students have to register at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency. Please find the instructions and timetable for the registration from
Student's cheklist
item number 14.
Persons from outside the Nordic and the EEA countries
Persons from outside the Nordic and the EEA countries who intend to stay in Finland for more than 3 months need a residence permit which should be acquired before arrival in Finland at the nearest Finnish embassy or consulate. Please see the Finnish Immigration Flowchart: Residence Permit for Studies at
www.migri.fi
.
Finnish Immigration Service Information for Students​​ - how to apply for the residence permit
Finnish Personal Identity Code
Every foreign student needs a Personal Identity Number. It is formed by your birthday and four digits, example 010192-000A. You will receive it from Digital and Population Data Service Agency.
Please find the instructions and timetable for the registration from
Student's checklist
item number 14.
Insurance
All students are responsible for their own insurance arrangements and we strongly recommend you to take a comprehensive insurance for your stay in Finland. Before leaving your home country, please check your travel and health insurance. Remember to bring the valid insurance policy with you!
As an exchange student your healthcare services in Finland are provided either through public or private sector depending on the country you come from and your insurances. It is also recommended that you have a valid health care insurance during your whole stay in Finland.
EU citizens: European Health Insurance Card & private insurance
Students from the EU/EEA countries are entitled to public health care services in Finland, if they are covered by health insurance in their own country.  More information about
Finland's public and private healthcare.
Make sure that you have your European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) with you.
A European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) is needed for public health care services in Finland. The card ensures that you will get the same access to public sector health care as the local residents (e.g. a doctor, a pharmacy, a hospital or a health care centre), covering mainly emergency treatment in the event of an illness or injury, and other medically necessary treatment. Any costs you incur outside the system you will have to pay on your own.
Citizens of the EU/EEA countries must also have a private insurance in addition to the European Health Insurance Card. The European Health Insurance Card is not valid during your travels to and from Finland and during any excursions to a third country outside of the EU.
Get more information about
European Health insurance card EHIC
and
European Commission
.
Students outside the EU: private insurance
Students from outside the EU/EEA must have private insurance to cover the duration of the visa / residence permit and the Schengen area before they enter Finland. More information about
Finland's public and private healthcare
.
Remember to bring the valid insurance policy with you.
The insurance must cover the treatment and health care provided by public health care services, cases of illness or accident, and include travel costs to home country as well as liability insurance.
Taking insurance from an international insurance company is recommended. For travel outside Finland, please make sure the insurance is valid in these countries as well.
More information about insurance from
Finnish Immigration Services
and
information about insurances for students coming to Finland.

Studies for exchange students
We offer studies for exchange students in all our study fields. All available courses for exchange students are taught in English and are usually second- or third-year studies.
The studies are offered by four faculties: Business and Hospitality Management, Health Care and Social Services, Technology and the Institute of Design and Fine Arts. Language studies are provided by the LAB language center.
In this section we have collected general information about studying at LAB
Academic year and orientation days
The academic year at LAB University of Applied Sciences is divided into autumn and spring semesters. Within these semesters each faculty has their own study period and course schedule. Exams are included in the study periods and there are no separate exam weeks.​
Academic year 2026/2027
The semester dates during the academic year 2026/2027 are listed below and they will be confirmed in the acceptance letter.
Autumn semester: ~ 24.8. - 19.12.2026 (Orientation starts 24.8.2026)
Spring semester: ~ 4.1. - 31.5.2027
Our Academic year dates will be updated to our
Student Calender webpage
.
Orientation days
The orientation days might be before the official semester dates, students will be notified about the orientation dates also once they receive their acceptance letters. The program of orientation days can be found from the
orientation pages
.
Autumn orientation: In the end of August / beginning of September
Spring orientation: On week two
Study Guidance
Providing support and guidance to you during your studies is one of our most important tasks. We want you to learn, achieve and develop your skills while you also enjoy studying with us.
The aim of the guidance is to help you achieve your targets with regards to your agreed study plan. Through this guidance process we hope that you will develop skills which will enable you to:
Adapt to the Finnish education system and teaching culture
Study independently and in teams
Develop your learning skills
Adapt to the Finnish working life during projects and work placements
And successfully complete studies planned for your student exchange period
Every degree programme has a dedicated Tutor Teacher (Departmental Coordinator). They will check your Learning Agreement upon your arrival and sign it. They are here to help you with questions regarding studies at LAB University of Applied Sciences.
Study Methods and Exams
The Finnish welfare society is built on education, culture and knowledge. Education is a key factor in enhancing Finnish competitiveness and therefore the key aims of the Finnish education policy are quality, efficiency, equity and internationalization.
The independent nature of UAS studies in Finland presupposes that students show initiative and take responsibility for the planning of their studies and for keeping to their own schedules. LAB being a university of applied sciences also means that the approach is very practical, including less theory and more projects.
The study methods at LAB University of Applied Sciences support self-guided development, which creates a basis for comprehensive learning: lectures, teamwork, projects, reading assignments and essays. In addition to face-to-face lectures, LAB also offers many online courses.
Please note that there is no specific exam period at the end of the term; exams are held throughout the academic year.
Learning Agreement
Please choose the courses for your Learning Agreement from the list of your study field. Exchange students are expected to complete 30 ECTS credits during the semester.
Erasmus+ students: Erasmus+ students' Learning Agreements are processed in Erasmus without papers network as data transfer. Erasmus+ students should therefore create Learning Agreement according to the instructions from their home institution in the system the home institution is using.
Non-Erasmus student: Non-Erasmus students should create a Learning Agreement in LAB Mobility-Online according to the instructions available on the platform.
Please note that LAB University of Applied Sciences will sign your Learning Agreement only after you have been accepted as an exchange student to LAB.​
Course Registration
Your Tutor Teacher (Departmental Coordinator) instructs you about the course registration. Please be prepared to make changes for your original study plan after the course schedules are published.
Assessment criteria
Assessment criteria for each course are specified in the Course Descriptions. At the beginning of each course, students will be informed on the assessment principles which must be based on the course objectives. LAB University of Applied Sciences has the following assessment scale:
5 Excellent - 4 Very good - 3 Good - 2 Satisfactory - 1 Sufficient - 0 Fail - HYV Pass -HYL Fail
Students who fail a course may re-sit the exam twice on specified dates. The grade of an approved course cannot be upgraded in a re-sit.
Students will be provided with feedback and assessment within four weeks after the course has finished and in any case well before the next possible retake. Grades for successfully completed courses that have been entered in the study credit register cannot be erased.
ECTS Credit System
Finnish higher education institutions use ECTS credit system. The estimated workload for full time student is 30 ECTS credits per semester. Please note that a credit does not refer to the duration of a course, but to the estimated amount of work required. One credit refers to approximately 27 hours of work by the student. Lectures, projects, assignments, and other forms of studies learning methods are all taken into consideration when the number of credits for each course is calculated.
Transcript of records
Students at LAB University of Applied Sciences have access to their study credit register where they can follow their up-to-date course performance. Official transcripts of records are provided by LAB University of Applied Sciences after all the grades have been given - approximately five weeks after the end of semester. Students will receive an email when their final transcript of records has been uploaded in the online system.
Courses for exchange students at LAB
Note! Due to technical issues with our study guide, course information is currently unavailable. We apologize for the inconvenience this may cause.
The courses for exchange students are available in the
online Study Guide
. Please note that the course descriptions, implementations, and timings can be updated in Study Guide later. (You should remember to change the language of the website to English using the button in the top left corner).
The majority of the chosen courses should be on-campus courses from the study field the student is applying for. Incoming exchange students may take some courses cross faculties and study fields if they meet the courses' prerequisites. However, please note that courses from the Institute of Design and Fine arts are available only for design and fine arts students. Note also that there can be changes in course offerings still in the beginning of the semester. Language and culture courses and interdisciplinary courses are open for all exchange students.

LAB exchange student comments from the field of study in previous years:
"I had a great time here at LAB with many great Exchanges students. What I liked about LAB is that it is all very accessible with the teachers. Teachers always want to help you where possible and think about solutions. Many lessons given are also genuinely interesting and the teaching material also keeps up with the times. Topics were also often discussed about what is currently going on in International Marketing, for example. You can choose from many different subjects, so there is something for everyone. What I also like about LAB is that it is also a kind of place where you can chill with your friends, has many places to do homework and also has nice facilities such as ping pong, pool tables and saunas. You can also exercise very cheaply in the gym, but you can also take group lessons, which is great that this is offered. I look back on my time at LAB with a good feeling, I had a very nice period."

Fall and Spring semester can be taken separately or combined in any order. Courses are taught in English by qualified lecturers and business professionals. By attending the International Business programme, the students gain knowledge and skills in the field of Business Administration. Come and study with us at LAB University of Applied Sciences in an innovative, international atmosphere!

Note! Due to technical issues with our study guide, course information is currently unavailable. We apologize for the inconvenience this may cause.

Courses are taught in English by qualified lecturers and business professionals. We have versatile learning environments in Lappeenranta campus, like Gastro Bar Saimaa, where facilities promote learning by doing. By attending the Tourism and Hospitality Management program, students gain knowledge and skills in the field of Tourism and Hospitality Management business, which open working opportunities in the tourism sector as well as restaurants and gastronomy. LAB exchange student comments from the field of study in previous years:
"In my field of study in Tourism and Hospitality Management at LAB, there are many international students, so we all naturally speak English. I also found that the teachers at LAB are really empowering and supportive.
Overall, the studies are more focused on the practical and group work. We typically have assignments and presentations instead of traditional exams. Studying and working on a group project with students from all around the world is an enriching experience. During hospitality-related courses we had the opportunity to get to know different cultures, diverse working habits and the most valuable skill we got, is the ability to effectively work in multicultural teams, which is especially important for the Hospitality Industry.
There are a lot of practical exercises such as organizing a Pop-up restaurant at Gastro Bar Saimaa that help to apply the theoretical knowledge into praxis. This helped to improve our skills in planning and organizing a restaurant, but I also to improve our customer service work with the guests.
The campus offerings restaurants and a café as well as the gym and different kinds of sport classes are a great way to finish a day of studying."

Digital Experience Design (Lahti campus)
Note! Due to technical issues with our study guide, course information is currently unavailable. We apologize for the inconvenience this may cause.
Digital experience design studies focus on developing a better and smoother digital everyday life and future. Digital technologies are constantly evolving, so the importance of skilled user-centered digital experience designers is also growing. The Digital Experience Design program teaches students to understand all the factors encountered in the digital world and to create a positive user experience from the sum of these factors.
In digital experience design studies you can specialize as a user interface and user experience designer, a digital concept expert, or a service designer in the digital world.
The study field of Digital Experience Design is combining the previous study fields of Media Content Design and User Experience and User Interface Design (UX/UI). You can find previous course catalogues from these study field below.

"As a digital media student at home, I did not think there would be many differences when studying in media content design in LAB. Students are given lots of material and assistance by the lecturers with a lot of time for the creative process. This time can be used by students to focus on even the little things and create a final product that is not only a good design but is well thought through with what materials are used, where it will be placed and many other smaller factors that are disregarded by those who are on tighter schedules and I believe this is what puts the students a cut above the rest. With this level of detail their works become a well thought out experience rather than just a piece of designed media. If I had not studied media content design LAB, I feel I would have also looked past these smaller details."

Product Development Engineering (Lappeenranta campus)
Your studies in the Open Engineering programme are directed by you, the student; the starting point is your personal learning goals and needs. Exchange students work together with degree students in international teams on real-life engineering projects that match their areas of study and fields of interest. The programme is a unique opportunity for you to develop practical skills and gain theoretical knowledge based on your own motivations. You will also practice abilities such as tackling challenges, collaboration, and design thinking, which will prove useful in your future career.
The degree programme builds on the foundation of Mechanical Engineering, but the challenges students tackle can relate to almost any field under the engineering umbrella—such as design, mechatronics, electronics or process engineering etc. Our facilities are well-equipped for designing and building various prototypes. The first step is to define your learning path through discussions with your coach. For exchange students, it is highly recommended to start thinking about your ideas before arriving on campus.
Students may choose to dedicate an entire semester to self-directed learning in the Open Engineering environment or additionally choose other courses and projects to support their learning process.
You will be working on a project based on the skills you want to improve during the exchange and will receive credits (for instance 15-35 ECTS credits) for the project course. You can
compare the programme to a project semester where you can define the topic.
Students may choose to dedicate an entire semester to self-directed learning in the Product Development Engineering environment or additionally choose other courses and projects to support their learning process.

) is a great place to do that. You can find a large variety of different machines and a young and pretty supportive team who is always available if there are any questions or you need help. Moreover, the structure of a classical lecture is also quite different as in my home country (Germany). You call everybody with their first name. Professors and lecturer were always available, at least per mail, and supportive. Studying felt pretty independent too on the other hand. I was allowed to study what I am really interested in, didn’t have an overload of inherent material. There was not a classical exam period at the end if the semester. I had several assignments during the semester and only few exams. You keep doing constantly small tasks, for me it felt way better than studying an insane amount at the end of the semester just for an exam period."
