Measures to help control infection for international students
Tweet
To support student health and infectious disease prevention, Institute of Science Tokyo requires all incoming international students, both degree-seeking and non-degree-seeking, to submit a health certificate and strongly recommends participation in the annual medical checkup.
Who should submit?
International students who have been admitted to the university and will be enrolled for three months or longer, including those transferring from universities, colleges of technology, or Japanese language schools in Japan.
*Not applicable to currently enrolled international students who were enrolled at Science Tokyo in the previous year and have already submitted Health Certificate Parts I and II.
Deadline
The required documents must be submitted before the enrollment date at Science Tokyo, or within three months prior to the planned date of arrival in Japan if arrival is after enrollment.
Examples:
Enrollment date: April 1 → Deadline: March 31
Enrollment date: October 1 → Deadline: September 30
Health Certificate
Download the form from the link below and have a physician at a medical institution in your home country complete it in English or Japanese within three months prior to your enrollment date at Science Tokyo (or your planned date of arrival in Japan, if you will arrive after enrollment).
Health-Certificate-Part1.pdf
Health-Certificate-Part2.pdf
Part I: Tuberculosis (TB) Screening
Must be submitted by international students
falling under 1. or 2. below.
They must undergo an Interferon Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) test and have a physician complete the form.
1. Individuals who were born in or stayed long term (more than 6 months) in
countries or territories that have a high incidence of active TB.
2. Individuals who have had close contact with persons known or suspected to have active TB.
Part II: Certificate of Vaccinations
Must be submitted by
ALL
international students. They must have a physician complete the form.
Important:
If you are unable to complete the required vaccinations before enrollment, receive the first dose in your home country and upload the record. Complete the remaining dose(s) after arriving in Japan and email proof of vaccination to the address below.
Please refer to the list of medical institutions below if you plan to be vaccinated in Japan.
See clinics where vaccinations are availablen in Japan.
Items to Be Included in the Health Certificate
Part Ⅰ:  Interferon Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) results (blood test)
Individuals from countries with a high incidence of tuberculosis (see link below)
are required to undergo an IGRA test within three months prior to their arrival in Japan.
Countries or territories that have a high incidence of active TB
Part Ⅱ:  Vaccine Preventable Diseases (VPDs)
Required for
All International Students
1. Measles, Mumps, Rubella, and Varicella
Provide one of the following for each disease:
● Antibody titer test result (with laboratory report)
● Record of two vaccine doses (with vaccination dates)
● History of infection (with documented date of diagnosis)
Notes:
・If your antibody test result is
negative or indeterminate
, you must consult a physician or travel clinic
and receive vaccination.
・Vaccinations without documentation will be considered
not received.
・ Science Tokyo recommends
completion of the standard vaccination schedule (two doses for each vaccine).
2. Tetanus
● Provide a record of tetanus vaccination received within the past 10 years.
● If you have not been vaccinated within the past 10 years, receive a tetanus-containing vaccine
(e.g., Tetanus Toxoid, Tdap, or Td).
● Antibody titer test results are not accepted in place of vaccination records.
● Tetanus Immune Globulin (TIG) is not accepted. A tetanus vaccine is required.
How to Submit the Health Certificate
Submit the health certificate from
this
system.
Please prepare all required documents before entering any information into the online system.  If you are unable to submit the documents through the online system, please contact us at the email address below.
Personal Information Protection
The collected personal information will be managed in compliance with all the laws and regulations regarding personal information for all students at Science Tokyo, and will not be used for any purposes other than those indicated in
the Policy on Protecting the Privacy of Students, Faculty, and Staff at the Health Support Center
Frequently Asked Questions
1. Is there a designated medical institution for the health certificate?
No. It is acceptable as long as it is completed in either English or Japanese by a physician.
2. Does the health certificate have to be completed in English, including the name and address of the medical institution?
The health certificate, including the name and address of the medical institution, must be completed either in Japanese or English.
3. Does the health certificate have to be stamped with a seal of the medical institution?
The health certificate should either be signed by the physician or stamped by the medical institution.
4. Is there financial assistance for vaccine shots in Japan?
No. You are responsible for the expenses.Also note that Japanese health insurance does not cover vaccinations.
5. Can I be exempt from submitting the health certificate?
No, it’s mandatory. If this is not followed, your academic supervisor will be notified.
6. I was a student at  Science Tokyo in the past( or I am a newly enrolled internal student)and have stayed in Japan since then.  Do I need to submit the health certificate?
Only if you did not submit it when you were previously enrolled.
7. In place of the IGRA test (blood test) for Part I, can I use the PPD test (tuberculin test) results?
The IGRA test is highly recommended as the PPD test is prone to false-positive and false-negative results. Only under the condition that there is no local medical institution providing an IGRA test AND you have never had a BCG(vaccination for TB)in the past, you may use PPD test result.
8. TB screening tests are pricey in my country. In Japan, is there financial assistance for students, or are there options that are less expensive?
No. We understand that tests are expensive. However, we ask for your cooperation in implementing measures to help control infection.
If IGRA testing is applicable to you, please undergo a test (costing about 10,000 yen in Japan) and submit a completed Part I form.
9. What should I do if I don’t have records?
If you do not have the records of immunization, do either A or B below.
A.　Take an antibody test and submit the lab report. If the antibody titer is below the acceptable level, consult the doctor for an additional shot.
B.　Get vaccinated for MMR, varicella, and tetanus.
For MMR and varicella, you should be vaccinated twice. If you only have one record of vaccination, you should also take the titer test at least two months after the previous vaccination and submit the lab report with PartⅡ.
Vaccination for tetanus must be done within the past 10 years.  If not, a booster is required.
10. I have my childhood vaccination record proving that required vaccinations have been completed. Can I skip Part II if I submit a copy of the record?
No. Have your physician complete Part II based on your vaccination record. If not, take the titer tests prove that you have immunity and complete the document.
11. I cannot get the required vaccination in my country.
Get vaccinated upon arrival in Japan. Enter “to be vaccinated upon arrival in Japan” in the Part II form, and upload the form online. Upon vaccination after your arrival, submit a receipt from the clinic via emai to notify the Healthcare Center Center that you have completed the vaccination.
12. Vaccination for tetanus is not available in my country.
Get vaccinated with Tetanus Diphtheria and Pertussis vaccines (Tdap or DTP), which also provide you with protection against Pertussis (whooping cough).  If neither of the vaccinations are available, follow the instructions written in  Q.11
13.  I am planning to receive the second dose of the vaccine in Japan but I received/will receive the first one in another country . My proof of vaccination is written in a language other than Japanese or English. Will I be able to use this?
No, if you get the first dose of the vaccine in another country, have the doctor fill out PartⅡ in English and upload the document online. After you get your second shot in Japan, follow the instruction written in Q.11.
14. I’ve finished all the vaccine shots. Do I still need to undergo an immune titer test for Part II?
If you only have one shot for MMR and for varicella, you need to take the antibody tests to confirm that you are immuned(positive) and submit the lab report as well. If the lab report is either negative or equivocal, you must consult the doctor for an additional shot.
15. Does Science Tokyo have specific recommendations for vaccine brands?
No. Consult your physician and do as advised.
16. Does Science Tokyo make arrangements for me to receive vaccine shots in Japan?
No. You need to do it by yourself.  Refer to 『travel-clinics.pdf』of this page for clinics available in Japan.

+81-3-5734-2065

title: 東京科學大學：東京科學官方：dorm-faq（116適用性待查）
text:
【網頁／無PDF頁碼】
Frequently Asked Questions
Frequently asked questions about applying for a student dormitory and living in a dormitory are listed below. Please read them before you apply.
About dormitory applications
Expand all
Q
I'd like to enter Tokyo Tech next spring and stay in a student dormitory. When do applications open?
A
We start accepting online applications from mid-January.
Q
Can I apply before the release of the entrance exam results?
A
Yes. However, you’ll lose your eligibility if you fail the exam.
Q
I’d like to secure a room in a dormitory in February, before the entrance exam results in March. Is that possible if I pay rent?
A
Not allowed. You can move in after the move-in date.
Q
Can I apply for more than one dormitory and indicate my first choice, second choice, etc.?
A
Applications will only be accepted for one dormitory. However, if you are unable to move into the dormitory you have applied for, we may be able to offer you another dormitory if one is available.
Q
Could my application be rejected? What’s the ratio of applications for dormitories?
A
Selection will be by lottery if the number of applications exceeds capacity.
The ratio of applications differs every year, depending on the dormitory.
Q
If my application is successful, can I choose my room? Can I request a room change after moving in?
A
You can’t choose your room or roommates, and room change requests are not accepted.
Q
Is there a charge for cancellation?
A
No cancellation fee will be charged.
Q
Will the initial fee be refunded when I leave?
A
The initial fee is not refundable.
Q
Can I view rooms before applying?
A
A Yes. Please contact the Student Support Division.
(No viewing available for Suzukakedai House and Minami-Tsukushino House)
Q
Can I keep my room while on a leave of absence or studying abroad? If yes, will I be charged rent?
A
Please inquire separately as it depends on the period and circumstances.
Q
What is the “reservation number” printed on my application form?
A
It’s a number for students enrolling in certain specified programs.
About dormitory life
Expand all
Q
Is there a curfew?
A
No curfew.
Q
Can my friends visit me in my room?
A
In principle, only residents are allowed to enter private rooms. Access to common areas is handled differently in each dormitory, so please inquire for details.
Q
May friends stay overnight?
A
Non-residents are not allowed to stay overnight.
Q
Are meals provided?
A
No, the dormitories aren’t catered.
Q
Is there a TV in the dormitory? If not, can I bring my own?
A
Private rooms are not equipped with a TV, but some dormitories have common rooms with one. Please consult us if you would like to bring your own.
Q
Can I access the internet in my room?
A
Internet service is available in the dormitory. No application is required.
Q
Is bedding provided?
A
Those in other dormitories have only a mattress. Please bring your own bedding set and linen, or purchase them from our supplier at a discount rate. (No purchasing available for Suzukakedai House and Minami-Tsukushino House)
Q
How do I pay the rent?
A
Payment methods differ depending on the dormitory. We’ll explain the relevant procedure to each student well before their residency starts.
Minamishinagawa House
Expand all
Q
Is the Minami-Shinagawa House located within cycling distance of the campus?
A
Yes. Some residents commute by bicycle.
Q
What appliances are provided in residential units?
A
There is a refrigerator, microwave.
Senzokuike House
Expand all
Q
Can I have a specific address?
A
Only if you’ve been assigned a room. Please contact us if you would like to view the facility.
Q
Can my friends visit me in the house?
A
Female visitors are allowed to visit, but may only enter the dining room and lounge.
Q
I’d like to ask my father to help me move in/out. Can he enter the dormitory?
A
He’ll be allowed to enter the dining room and lounge on the first floor only. Please follow the rules about visitors.
Midorigaoka House
Expand all
Q
Are undergraduate students accepted?
A
No, the Midorigaoka House is exclusively for graduate students.
Nagatsuta House
Expand all
Q
Is there a shuttle bus to the campus?
A
Yes, there’s a free shuttle bus that for only Nagatsuta House residents  between the dormitory and Suzukakedai Campus — three times in the morning and evening. It takes about 10 minutes.
Unfortunately, Nagatsuta House residents are not allowed to ride bicycles to school.
Komaba Dormiory, Shofu  Dormiory and Umegaoka Dormiory
Expand all
Q
I’m a new international student. Can I apply for an international dormitory?
A
New international students and exchange students who have received an invitation to move in from the Student Support Division and have a reservation number may apply.
Q
How can I get a reservation number?
A
If you have a reservation number, yes. We send information about dormitories along with a reservation number to eligible international students.
Q
Can Japanese students reside in the dormitory?
A
Only those assigned as dormitory tutors will be permitted and may be able to move in when recruited.

text:
【第1頁】
2026/01/15 
 
CALL FOR APPLICATION  
TOKYO INTERNATIONAL EXCHANGE CENTER (TIEC)  
<Nomination System 2026 > 
 
1. Application Requirements for international students: 
(1) Current graduate students with outstanding study record, who have student visa status, and can commute 
from the TIEC to campus. Prospective students who are admitted by Science Tokyo are also eligible to 
apply. (They may move-in 30 days prior to the enrollment.) (Please submit a photocopy of acceptance 
letter with your application form.) 
* No qualification for those who are taking, or will take a leave of absence. 
* No qualification for those who have extended or extend their term of study. 
(2) Students who participate in exchange programs (graduate course level) held by Institute of Science Tokyo 
for more than 30 days. Those students who don’t have student visa status are also eligible to apply. 
(3) Residence period is within 1 year (It is extendable up to 3 years if it is within the term of study and 
JASSO approves it). JASSO approves it after review about applicants’ attendance to TIEC events, and their 
behavior while living in TIEC. 
If the term of study is until August 2026, the residence period ends by August 25, 2026. If the term of study 
is until September 2026, the residence period ends by September 25, 2026. If the term of study is until 
March 2027, the residence period ends by March 25, 2027. 
(4) As room assignments are made through university recommendation, we kindly ask that you refrain 
from canceling after receiving approval for residence. Please take this into careful consideration 
when submitting your application.   
 
2. Document Required: 
(1) Application for Tokyo International Exchange Center (Form 1)   
(2) The proposal for implementation / participation of exchange activities at TIEC (Form 3)

cohabitants) or official certificate shows relationship between you and your cohabitants, written in English or 
Japanese.

International student guide
This guide compiles necessary and useful information for international students regarding life in Japan and studying at Science Tokyo. There are unique systems and procedures specifically for international students, so when you're in doubt or trouble, first use this guide to collect the information you need.
International student guide
This international student guide contains important information for your studies at Science Tokyo. Since there are certain systems and procedures specific to international students, please refer to it as needed.
The guide is only available in English.
Table of contents
1. Residence Status and Registration Procedures
2. Visa Consulting Service
3. Japanese Health and Social Insurance Systems

1. Residence Status and Registration Procedures
1.1 Residence Card
1.2 Registration of Address Information
1.3 Change in Information on the Residence Card Other than Place of Residence
1.4 Social Security and Tax Number (Individual Number)
1.5 Procedures to Be Taken before Traveling Overseas from Japan
1.6 When Taking a Leave of Absence
1.7 When Studying Abroad
1.8 When Undertaking an Internship in/outside Japan
1.9 When Graduating from Science Tokyo/ Completing a Degree Program
1.10 When Withdrawing/ Being Expelled from Science Tokyo
1.11 Extension of Period of Stay
1.12 Applying for Permission to Engage in Activity Other than That Permitted under the Status of Residence Previously Granted
1.1 Residence Card
A residence card is issued at the port of entry to persons entering Japan who have been granted residence status with a period of stay of three or more months. Please carry your residence card with you at all times.
1.2 Registration of Address Information
(1) Notification of Place of Residence (registration of residence)
After entering Japan, international students are required to report their place of residence to local municipal offices without delay. Submit a Notification of Place of Residence to the office for registration of your residency within 14 days after moving in.
(2) Procedures to Be Taken When Changing Residence
a. Notify the local municipal or ward office
Whenever you move to a new residence, you are required to notify your local municipal or ward office of the change of address within 14 days after moving in.
b. Notify the Student Division and the Student Support Division
Science and engineering students
Bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral students:
Please change your address on the website (Web System for Students and Faculty).
Additionally, please bring your residence card with the new address to Student Support Division for scanning.
Research Students, International Exchange Students, International Visiting Students, Japanese Intensive Course Students:
Please bring your residence card with the new address to Student Support Division for scanning.
Medical and dental sciences students
Undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, and research students:
Please submit a copy of both sides of your updated residence card that lists the new address to the Student Support Division at Yushima Campus via the following link:
- Reporting Your Residence Status "Student"
c. Change the address registered on your National Health Insurance Card.
Once you have changed your address, you can no longer use the National Health Insurance Card issued with your former address. To change the address, complete the required procedures at the local municipal or ward office for your new address without delay. Please bring your old National Health Insurance Card with you.
d. Change the address registered on your bank account.
Please notify your bank of any change of address. Bring your bankbook to the bank where it was issued and have the address updated. If scholarship recipients fail to do so, their scholarships may not be credited appropriately.
e. Notify the post office.
To receive letters and mail addressed to your former address at your new place, request a mail forwarding service at a post office. Fill in and submit the prescribed form which is available at any post office, and mail will be forwarded to your new address for up to one year. Note that mail cannot be forwarded to overseas addresses; forwarding addresses must be in Japan. Please also note that forwarded mail will take longer to reach you than normal, since it takes some time to redirect mail to a different address.
1.3 Change in Information on the Residence Card Other than Place of Residence
If there is any change in the information on the residence card other than the address (e.g., name, date of birth, sex, nationality/region) or termination of the “Student” status of residence (e.g., graduation, withdrawal, etc.), mid-to-long-term residents must report it to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of the change. Bring your residence card to the nearest office and complete the necessary procedures. Failing to do so may result in penalties or revocation of status of residence. Once the necessary procedures are completed, a new residence card will be issued.
After receiving your new residence card with the updated information, please notify the Student Support Division.
1.4 Social Security and Tax Number (Individual Number)
In accordance with the Social Security and Tax Number System (My Number System), all registered residents of Japan are issued a twelve-digit individual number. This number will be required for various types of administrative procedures, including social security and tax procedures, as well as disaster countermeasures. This number is very important for managing personal information, so please do not throw it away or show it to other persons. It is valid for life. The same number will be issued when leaving and re-entering Japan.
1.5 Procedures to Be Taken before Traveling Overseas from Japan
Science and engineering students
Notify the Global Education Division.
Regular students
Please submit an “Overseas Travel Notice” via Rakrak WF II. For more information, please visit the following website.
Procedures for Study Abroad and Other Overseas Travel
Non-regular students
Please submit an “Overseas Travel Notice” via Microsoft Forms using the link below.
- International exchange students and international visiting students
- Non-regular students who are not international exchange or visiting students
Medical and dental sciences students
Notify the Student Support Division.
All students
Please submit a “Temporary Leave Notice” via Microsoft Forms using the link below here:
Temporary Leave Notice
Whenever you travel outside Japan (including travel for vacations and travel to your home country), please ensure that you have travel insurance.
1.6 When Taking a Leave of Absence
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to take a leave of absence.
If you take a leave of absence, you cannot remain in Japan under "Student" status, nor are you allowed to work part-time. You must leave Japan promptly or change to an appropriate residence status if you wish to stay.
If you are going to take a leave of absence for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport. You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to resume studying at Science Tokyo. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
1.7 When Studying Abroad
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to study abroad.
If you are going to study abroad for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to re-enter Japan. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
1.8 When Undertaking an Internship in/outside Japan
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to undertake internships.
If you undertake an internship abroad for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to re-enter Japan. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
If you are going to undertake an internship in Japan, see the Immigration Services Agency's website and apply for permission as necessary.
For those wishing to apply for an internship | Immigration Services Agency
1.9 When Graduating from Science Tokyo/ Completing a Degree Program
The "Student" status is only valid during your period of enrollment at Science Tokyo. After graduation or completion, you must leave Japan promptly, even if your period of stay still remains valid. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
If your period of stay includes extra time beyond your enrollment for departure preparation, (i.e., if your residence period is significantly longer than your period of enrollment), you cannot change to "Temporary visitor" status for the purpose of such preparation.
If you plan to stay in Japan after graduation/completion, you must change to an appropriate status (see below for examples) and submit a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)" to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of graduation/completion, unless you continue your studies at Science Tokyo.
Immigration Services Agency website for a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)"
If you are planning to start work: contact the company where you have received a job offer (Naitei) and change your status to "Working."
If you already have a job offer (Naitei) from a company and want to stay in Japan until your job starts: contact the company and change your status to "Designated Activities (Naitei Taiki)."
If you want to continue job hunting (regular students only): contact the Student Support Division and apply for a change of status to "Designated Activities (Job Hunting)."
If you have a letter of acceptance to a graduate school and want to stay until the date of enrollment: contact the Student Support Division and apply for a change of status to "Designated Activities (Shingaku Taiki)."
1.10 When Withdrawing/ Being Expelled from Science Tokyo
If you withdraw or are expelled from Science Tokyo, you cannot remain in Japan under "Student" status and must leave Japan promptly. When departing, please return your residence card at the airport.
If you plan to stay in Japan to enroll at another university or to work in Japan, please check your status with your new university or company. You must also submit a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)" to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of the date of withdrawal/expulsion.
Immigration Services Agency website for a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)"
1.11 Extension of Period of Stay
Undergraduate international students who have acquired less than 25 credits over the past year may not be granted permission to renew their period of stay. (For medical and dental science students, this applies to those who have not acquired the required credits for advancement to the next academic year.)
For details, refer to the Science Tokyo website
Find the application procedures and necessary documents for extending your stay or changing your status of residence. Please check the relevant contact points according to your field below.
Science and engineering students
Students affiliated with the Ookayama Campus:
Open Science Tokyo Slack
Students affiliated with the Yokohama Campus:
Open Science Tokyo Slack
Medical and dental sciences students
Visit website
1.12 Applying for Permission to Engage in Activity Other than That Permitted under the Status of Residence Previously Granted
If international students must find a part-time job to pay for their studies or other expenses, they must receive permission to engage in activity other than that permitted under the status of residence previously granted (“Extra-status Activity”) by following the procedures prescribed by the Ministry of Justice. International students are allowed to work up to 28 hours per week (up to 8 hours per day during extended breaks).
If you engage in a part-time job without obtaining permission, your current visa status may be revoked. Furthermore, you may not apply for permission for certain types of jobs (those related to the adult entertainment industry, cleaning duties in pachinko parlors, etc.). Note that TAs, RAs, and tutors employed by Science Tokyo do not need to obtain this permission.
Required Documents
Application Form
The application form can be downloaded from the following link:
APPLICATION FOR PERMISSION TO ENGAGE IN ACTIVITY OTHER THAN THAT PERMITTED UNDER THE STATUS OF RESIDENCE PREVIOUSLY GRANTED
Passport (original)
Residence card (original)
Where to Apply
Applicants can submit the documents either to the Visa Consulting Service staff or directly to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau.
If you use the Visa Consulting Service, bring a copy of your passport and Residence Card with you.
Application Processing Time
Two weeks to one month
2. Visa Consulting Service
Science Tokyo has launched the Immigration and Visa Consulting Service to support international students and researchers with application procedures that concern international residents. On designated days, professionals from a law office will be available at the Student Support Division at Ookayama Campus and Yokohama Campus (Suzukake Hall, H1, H2 Bldg., Floor 2) and at the Yushima Student Support Office at Yushima Campus (Building 5, Floor 3). We invite you to make use of this service at your convenience.
Through this service, you no longer need to go to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau for most types of applications. Consultation is free of charge, but you will need to pay a commission if you use the application service. You are required to make a reservation in advance, and to bring your student ID card every time you use this service. (Your student visa must be valid for at least another 2 weeks.)
Details of when the service is available will be announced at:
Immigration & Visa Consulting Service
Reservation page
【Available Services】
Certificate of Eligibility (Student, Researcher, Professor, Dependent)
Extension of visa duration (Student, Researcher, Professor, Dependent)
Change of status
Re-entry permit
Permission to engage in a part-time job
3. Japanese Health and Social Insurance Systems
3.1 Join the National Health Insurance System
3.2 Apply for National Pension Contribution Special Payment System for Students
3.1 Join the National Health Insurance System
International students planning to reside in Japan for more than three months are required to join the National Health Insurance System at their local municipal or ward office. Although students must pay insurance premiums, they will only have to pay 30% of medical expenses while under the health insurance coverage.
Insurance premiums differ according to the ward or city, but the basic amount is approximately JPY 30,000 per year. If your annual income is low, you may be entitled to a reduction by applying at your local municipal or ward office, which must be done every year. Typically, the reduced premium is approximately JPY 10,000 per year, but it varies depending on the municipality or ward.
Note: Reimbursement for High-Cost Medical Care Payments
If your share of medical expenses incurred in a single calendar month exceeds a certain threshold, you may be eligible for reimbursement for high-cost medical care payments. The threshold varies depending on factors related to your income and age, but for most people, it is around JPY 35,400. To apply, submit an application to your local municipal office, attaching your National Health Insurance Card, receipts issued by the hospitals or pharmacies, and a detailed statement of medical expenses. Application reviews typically take two to three months, but processing times can vary. For details, consult the municipal office or ward office in your area.
3.2 Apply for National Pension Contribution Special Payment System for Students
All people between the ages of 20 and 59 who have a registered address in Japan must be covered by the National Pension system and must pay contributions, regardless of nationality or length of stay. If your income in Japan from the previous year is equal to or less than a specified amount, you may apply for the Special Payment System for Students to request a postponement of contribution payments. You need to file an application for each year with the municipal or ward office. By undergoing this procedure, you establish valid coverage periods that count toward the eligibility requirements for receiving future old-age pension benefits, as well as current benefits if you are accidentally injured and become disabled. For details, visit the Japan Pension Service website, where a sample of the application is available in English.
For details
4．Student Insurance
- Personal Accident Insurance for Students Pursuing Education and Research (Gakkensai)
- Personal Liability Insurance for Students (Futaibaiseki, Gakkenbai, or Igakubai)
All Science Tokyo students are expected to purchase certain insurance policies.
Personal Accident Insurance for Students Pursuing Education and Research (Gakkensai) provides financial assistance to students injured in accidents/disasters during studies, lab work, extracurricular activities, or commuting to or from campus.
Personal Liability Insurance for Students (Gakkenbai, Futaibaiseki Course A) covers costs for property damage or injuries to third parties resulting from accidents during most official Science Tokyo activities.
Science and engineering students are required to enroll in Gakkensai and Gakkenbai.
Medical and dental sciences undergraduate students
are required to enroll in Gakkensai. Depending on your affiliated school, you may also have to enroll in an additional liability insurance policy that covers accidents during medical or clinical training known as Igakubai (Futaibaiseki Course C).

4.4 Enrolling in the Insurance
Science and engineering student
Please use the e-shiharai service to pay your insurance premium during enrollment. If you enroll without paying, promptly collect a payment slip from the Student Support Division and pay the premium. Medical and dental sciences students
Pay insurance premiums to the bank account designated by Science Tokyo. Students who are advancing to a higher degree or changing programs (such as from a master’s to a doctorate, or from being a researcher to becoming a master’s student) need to go through the application procedure again. As a general rule, students must enroll in the insurance before starting their studies at Science Tokyo. Insurance premium payments are not accepted via overseas remittance, and international students are required to complete payment and necessary procedures immediately after arriving in Japan.
4.5 Claiming Insurance
Science and engineering students
Should you be involved in any of the abovementioned accidents, please notify the Student
Support Division immediately. We will provide you with the necessary support to claim indemnity.
If you have any questions, please contact the Student Support Division (email: studentinsurance.se(at)adm.isct.ac.jp).
Medical and dental sciences students
Please email the Student Support Division (studentinsurance.md(at)adm.isct.ac.jp).
4.6 Car Insurance
All cars and motorcycles must be covered by the compulsory automobile liability insurance. As
it only covers compensation for third parties for bodily injury in the case of an accident and does
not cover property damage or injury to the driver, it is highly recommended that voluntary
automobile insurance be obtained.
5. Medical Checkup
5.1 Medical Checkup and Medical Certificate
5.2 Special Medical Examination
5.1 Medical Checkup and Medical Certificate
The medical checkup is offered to all students in spring in order to help them find and prevent
any health-related problems. Please make sure to get it done every year.
Students entering in fall are required to undergo the fall checkup of that year, and in the spring
of the following year. For dates and other information, please visit the website below:
Science and engineering students
Medical and dental sciences students (Only in Japanese)
Students who require a medical certificate for scholarships, employment, dormitories, advancing
to another degree program, etc. must undergo the medical checkup.
A copy of the medical certificate can be obtained as below. However, the medical certificate does not apply to students who did not take the medical checkup for that year. For any questions, please contact the Student Healthcare Center.
Science and engineering students
A copy of the medical certificate can be obtained from an automated certificate issuance machine.
Medical and dental sciences students
A copy of the medical certificate can be requested at the Yushima Student Healthcare Center.
5.2 Special Medical Examination
Undergraduate students in their fourth year and above, graduate students, and any research
students who are exposed to ionized radiation and organic solvents in labs are recommended
to undergo a special medical examination that takes place in the spring and fall. If this applies
to you, please coordinate with your supervisor. Note that this medical examination is different
from the medical checkup explained above.

The Student Guidance Room and Student Support Center provides guidance and counseling
to help students deal with various problems such as school work, future careers, interpersonal

members on each campus are assigned as advisors. Please feel free to contact the Student

6.2 Student Life Coach Consultations
Student Life Coaches offer support on all aspects of your academic life. Please visit us if you
have any concerns regarding your campus life, course selection, or study plans. Consultations
are available in English.
How to arrange a consultation
Face-to-face consultation:
Please visit either the counter on Floor B1 of Taki Plaza or the Student Life Coach Room on the
first floor of the Suzukakedai Library. Reservations are not necessary. Please feel free to stop by
at any time during our office hours.
Consultation via email or Zoom:
Please send us your name, student ID number, affiliated School, Department, or graduate major,
and the topic for consultation by email to the address below. If you would like to have an online
consultation, please provide a few dates/time slots that suit your schedule by email. We will

questions or concerns you may have, such as:

6.4 Student Accessibility Services
Student Accessibility Services ensures that students with disabilities have full access to education and university life at Science Tokyo. If you are experiencing difficulties and require support, please call, email, or visit our office.
Any information provided during consultations will not be disclosed to third parties without the prior consent of the individual concerned.

and email. If you have a problem but find it difficult to visit other help desks, please call or email
the Telephone Consultation Service. Face-to-face and Zoom meetings can also be provided
whenever necessary. Privacy is strictly protected.

10．Commuter Passes and Student Discounts
Commuter passes, which may be good for a period of one, three, or six months, are a form of discounted travel. There are two kinds of commuter passes: student commuter passes and ordinary commuter passes. The cost of a student commuter pass is lower than that of an ordinary commuter pass.
10.1 Regular Students (degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students)
10.2 Non-Regular Students (Graduate Research Students, International Exchange Students, and International Visiting Students)
10.1 Regular Students (degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students)
Regular students (degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students) are eligible for a student commuter pass. You will be requested to show a Commuter Pass Purchase Certificate (Tsuugaku-teikiken-kounyu-shoumeisho) and your student ID card when purchasing the pass. Under Japanese law, Commuter Pass Purchase Certificates can only be issued for the least expensive route between the station nearest your home and the station nearest your campus. Hence, you will not be able to purchase a student commuter pass to travel to your part-time job or other destinations.
Commuter Pass Purchase Certificates are issued (the number of copies is limited) from automated certificate issuance machines at the Ookayama and Yokohama campuses. They are issued at the counter at Yushima Campus. Note that your student ID card is required, so you must collect it in person. You will need to keep the Certificate after using it to purchase a commuter pass, as it will be valid for the duration of your enrollment.
Regular students can also buy discounted student tickets. (Discounted student tickets are for journeys over 100 km one-way on JR lines, and cost 20 percent less than the regular fare. For details, please ask the staff at any JR station.) When purchasing a discounted student ticket, you will be requested to show a Student Discount Certificate (Gakuwarishou) and your student ID card. You can get the Student Discount Certificate from an automated certificate issuance machine.
10.2 Non-Regular Students (Graduate Research Students, International Exchange Students, and International Visiting Students)
Non-regular students are permitted to purchase a student commuter pass for Tokyu lines only.
Non-regular students cannot purchase discounted student tickets.

16.1 Eligibility
Students who enrolled in a doctoral degree program (science and engineering fields) in or after April 2018 are eligible to apply.
Doctoral students are not eligible if any of the following is true:
1. They receive financial aid from programs that do not permit funding from other sources (e.g.,
recipients of the JSPS Research Fellowship for Young Scientists, MEXT Scholarship students,
recipients of overseas government scholarships, Science Tokyo Program for Development of
Next-Generation Front-Runners with Comprehensive Knowledge and Humanity (Science Tokyo
SPRING), Science Tokyo Program for Development of Co-creative Experts towards Top-level AI
Research (Science Tokyo BOOST)).
2. They receive income as working adults (e.g., regular employees of a company, individuals who
own a business).
3. They have exceeded the standard duration of their doctoral studies.
16.2 Scholarship Amount
Scholarship amount (annual)
1st-year doctoral students
JPY 480,000 (standard scholarship)
2nd- and 3rd-year doctoral students
JPY 480,000 (standard scholarship)
Or JPY 635,400 (special scholarship*)
*Students who show outstanding academic performance and research achievements will be
granted a special scholarship in their second and/or third years. Approximately 20% of second
and third-year scholarship recipients will receive the special scholarship.

17.4 Traffic Rules in Japan
Lately, the number of the bicycle accidents has greatly increased. Please be aware of traffic
rules as accidents can have a devastating impact on the lives of those involved.
National police agency website “Traffic safety guidelines for pedestrians and cyclists”
Traffic Safety Rules
(1) Anti-theft registration
When riding a bicycle at night, you may be stopped by police who will ask to see your residence
card or other form of identification and check if you have a bicycle anti-theft registration sticker.
If the police find that the bicycle is registered in someone else’s name, you may be detained at
a police box for a long time, and possibly even charged with theft. To avoid this unpleasant
experience, take the following precautions:
・When purchasing a bicycle, be sure to register it at the store.
・If you receive a bicycle from a friend, fill out a “transfer of ownership” certificate together,
then take the document to a bicycle dealer to re-register the bicycle in your name.
・Never ride an abandoned bicycle.
(2) Automobile, motorcycle, and bicycle insurance
◆ Automobile and motorcycle insurance
If you plan to drive a car or ride a motorcycle, be sure to enroll in automobile or motorcycle insurance, since causing a traffic accident could make you liable to pay a large amount of compensation to any victims. Even if you only intend to drive or ride during a summer vacation trip or other short-term occasion, we strongly recommend that you buy insurance. Insurance policies can be purchased directly from an insurance company or through the University Co-op.
◆ Bicycle insurance
In many areas, including Tokyo and Kanagawa, it is mandatory to have insurance that covers liability if you injure someone in a bicycle accident. Insurance policies can be purchased directly from an insurance company or through the University Co-op.

Suzukakedai Campus renamed Yokohama Campus on April 1, 2026
April  1, 2026
Announcements
About Science Tokyo
Co-creating with society
Science Tokyo has changed the name of its Suzukakedai Campus to "Yokohama Campus," effective April 1, 2026.
Since its establishment in 1975, this campus has continued its educational and research activities for over half a century in northern Yokohama. Nestled in a lush green environment, it has produced numerous research achievements and progressed hand in hand with the local community.
The new campus name expresses Science Tokyo’s respect for the history of educational and research activities conducted in collaboration with the City of Yokohama, and the Institute’s determination to continue contributing to the development of the city.
The name "Suzukakedai" will continue to be used for certain facilities and events, such as Suzukakedai Library and Suzukake Science Day.
Having surpassed its 50th anniversary, Yokohama Campus is now taking a new step forward. While maintaining strong ties with the local community, it will fulfill its role as an important part of Science Tokyo as a University for International Research Excellence and return its achievements to society.

Tutors for international students
New international students arriving in Japan face various challenges and difficulties as they begin their new life, such as differences in language and lifestyle. Therefore, Science Tokyo has established a tutoring system for international students, where current students support new international students to smoothly settle in Japan and improve their academic and research outcomes. This system also aims to enhance the international understanding, cross-cultural awareness, and interest in international cooperation among the students serving as tutors.
What tutors shall do for new students
The support needed varies depending on the individual situation of each international student. To respond to the diverse needs of the students, tutors should proceed by confirming what kind of support is necessary for their assigned student. Here are some examples of support:
Examples of Support in Daily Life
Explaining Japanese culture and customs
Assisting with opening a bank account
Helping with procedures at city hall (residence registration, enrollment in National Health Insurance)
Assisting with shopping
Accompanying to hospitals
Examples of Academic Support
Introducing on-campus facilities (various offices, the library, classrooms, the Healthcare Center, etc.)
Providing support in laboratories
Assisting with course registration
Overview of the International Student Tutor System
Students hired by Science Tokyo as tutors provide support for the academic and daily lives of their assigned international students. For details on the hiring process, job duties, and reporting of working hours for tutors, please refer to the guidelines for your field below.

Airport arrival
Airport arrival
Arrival at the Airport
You will first arrive in Japan at one of the following airports: Fukuoka Airport (FUK), New Tokyo International Airport (NRT), Kansai International Airport (KIX), Central Japan International Airport (NGO), or Kumamoto Airport.
* If you arrive at New Tokyo International Airport (NRT), Kansai International Airport (KIX), or Central Japan International Airport (NGO), you should apply for transportation to Fukuoka Airport or Kumamoto Airport.
* If you arrive at Fukuoka Airport, we recommend you to take a highway bus from Fukuoka Airport or Hakata Bus Center to SAKURAMACHI Kumamoto Bus Terminal. This connection takes about two hours and costs approximately 2,500 yen. Before you leave Fukuoka, you should call your contact person at Kumamoto University and tell him/her your time of arrival at Kumamoto.
* If you arrive at Kumamoto Airport, you should take an airport limousine bus from Kumamoto Airport to SAKURAMACHI Kumamoto Bus Terminal. This connection takes about 50 minutes and costs 1000 yen.

Important Things to Do After Arriving in Kumamoto
Important Things to Do After Arriving in Kumamoto
Important Things to Do After Arriving in Kumamoto
Please read the "Handbook for International Students" carefully.
In addition, you should go through the following necessary procedures as soon as possible.
Your tutor or the staff at the International Student Office will help you to do them.
Notification (Change) of place of residence
Register for National Health Insurance
Register for National Pension System
Establish a bank account
Notification concerning the organization to which the foreigner belongs
In addition, those receiving Monbukagakusho (Japanese government, MEXT) scholarships should establish a postal saving account to receive scholarship.
1. Notification (Change) of Place of Residence
Foreigners who reside in Japan must go through notification (change) of place of residence within 14 days of finding a place to setlle down.
Please fill out the "Jyumin-Idoutodoke" form and submit it to the Kumamoto City Kuyakusho (Ward Office) along with your passport and residence card.
2. Registering for National Health Insurance
Foreign students who live in Japan longer than three months must register for National Health Insurance. Under the National Health Insurance plan, the Japanese government will cover 70% of your medical expenses if you get sick while in Japan. Please submit "Change in status/eligibility for National Health Insurance" and "Application for National Health Insurance" to Kumamoto City Kuyakusho (Ward Office). You need to notify when your address changed, brought your family to Japan or a baby is born. Please proceed to cancel your health insurance when you go back to your country.
3. Register for National Pension System
Not only Japanese citizens, but also foreign students over 20 years old must register for National Pension. You can complete the procedure for this at National Pension Section on Kumamoto City Kuyakusho (Ward Office) when you register for National Health Insurance. If your income is considered to be less than a pre-detemined income level, your insurance fee may be waived. Degree-seeking students (undergraduates and graduate school students) should apply for a "special exemption to student payment (Gakusei nofu tokurei)" and Non-degree seeking students (ex. special audit students, special research students) should apply for a "payment waiver (Menjo)".
4. Establishing a bank account
You can deposit money and transfer it to others. Both Higo Bank and Kumamoto Bank are located close to Kumamoto University.
In order to open up an account at a bank, you first need to fill out an account application form available at the bank. Please submit the form along with your passport and Certificate of Residence. It is usually necessary to have a name seal (called "inkan" in Japanese) when opening a bank account in Japan. For details, please visit
"Finance"
.
5. Notification concerning the organization to which the foreigner belongs
Students who belonged to another school in Japan such as university or language school before enrolling in Kumamoto University have to notify to the Ministry of Justice by visiting a Regional Immigration Office or sending a notification to the Tokyo Regional Immigration Bureau, within 14 days. You can notify on
the web
also.
*Attention Japanese Government Scholarship Students:
Please tell your postal savings account number to the international Affairs Division by designated date. Stipends for Japanese Government scholarship students are paid into postal savings accounts.
*Attention JASSO Scholarship Exchange Students:
Please tell your bank account number to the international Affairs Division by designated date.
Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
All international students at Kumamoto University have "College Student" visa status. You must apply for a permit to the Immigration Bureau through the International Student Office when you want to extend your stay, work part-time, bring your family to Japan, or re-enter Japan. In those cases, you should submit the forms for these permits to the International Student Office.

Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
Certificate of Eligibility
International Students who will enroll in Kumamoto University need to apply for a Certificate of Eligibility. It takes about a month to issue it.
You must submit the following documents:
For privately funded students:
Application for Certificate of Eligibility (College Student)
One photo taken within 6 months (4 cm × 3 cm, with no hats on and no background scenery)
A copy of the Certificate of Admission
A financial statement (certficate of scholarship, certificate of bank balance, or a copy of bankbook)
A copy of passport
If you would like to bring your family members to Japan:
Application for Certificate of Eligibility (Dependent) (one for each family member)
One photo taken within 6 months (4 cm × 3 cm, with no hats on and no background scenery)
Postal stamps for the required amount.
Proof of Relationship
If you bring your husband or wife to Japan: Certificate of marriage
If you bring your children to Japan: Birth certificates for children
A copy of your Regidence Card (both sides)
Proof of ability to support your family members who are coming to Japan
In the case of Japanese government scholarship students: Certificate of Scholarship
In the case of privately funded students: Certificate of bank balances or copy of bank book
Certificate of Student Status
A copy of your and your dependants' passports

Tuition fee exemption
There is a tuition fee exemption system for students with financial difficulties. Full exemption and half exemption are available. These can be applied for the academic year following entrance to the university, but it is not guaranteed that the fees will be exempted. The application period every year is around February for the whole year and around July for the second semester. Please confirm the exact dates with the Student Life Division. Research students and non-regular students are not eligible to apply for tuition fee exemption.

Finance
Finance
Bank
You must submit the following items for opening a bank account:
1) Application form for opening a bank account
2)
Inkan
(Name Seal) or your signatureWhen opening an account, you usually need an inkan (your own name seal).International students don't necessarily need an inkan. Instead, your signature will suffice.
3) Passport
4) Certificate of Residence or Resident Card
The nearest banks from the university are Higo Bank, Kokai-bashi Branch.
- Higo bank, Kokai-bashi Branch
Office Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
(closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and national holidays)
Phone: (096) 343-2185
Post Office
You can send letters, packages, as well as make deposits and remit money at the post office. In regards to scholarships being received from the Japan Student Services Organization (a.k.a. JASSO) (which includes Japanese Government Scholarship Students, Japan-Korea Joint Government Scholarship Program to the students in Science and Engineer Departments Science and Engineering students, and Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students), JASSO pays scholarships directly into recipients' postal savings accounts. Therefore, please create a postal savings account if above-mentioned scholars have not done so already.
You must submit the following for opening a postal savings account:
1) Application form for creation a postal savings account
2) Inkan (Name Seal) or your signatureWhen opening an account, you usually need an inkan (your own name seal). International students don't necessarily need an inkan. Instead, your signature will suffice.
3) Passport
4) Certificate of Residence or Resident Card
The nearest post office from Kumamoto University is Kurokami-daini Post Office.
- Kurokami-daini Post Office
Office Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
(closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and national holidays)
Phone: (096) 343-2672

Getting to the International House
Getting to the International House
1.Kurokammi South Campus:
Administrative Office, Faculty of Science, Faculty of Engineering, Graduate School of Science and Technology, Center for Multimedia and Information Technologies, Center for Marine Environment Studies, Shock Wave and Condensed Matter Research Center
2.Kurokami North Campus
International Student Center
Student's Office, Health Care Center, Faculty of Letters, Faculty of Education, Faculty of Law, Research Center for University Education, University Library, University School for Disabled Children
3.Honjo and Kuhonji Campuses
Faculty of Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
Graduate School of Medical Sciences
School of Medicine
School of Health Sciences
Institute of Resource Development and Analysis
Center for AIDS Research
Institute of Molecular Embryogy and Genetics
4.Honjo Campus
University Hospital
5.Oe Campus
Faculty of Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences School of Pharmacy Graduate School of Pharmaceutical Sciences
6.International House Building C-E
7.International House Building A-B
From Kumamoto Station:
By Sanko-Bus: take a bus for Ozu (via Sanrigi and Jinnai) and get off at the "Ozeki-bashi Bus Stop."
By JR train: From Kumamoto Station, take the Hohi Line and get off at "Tatsudaguchi Station" and then walk to the International House on foot.
By Taxi: Approximately 15 minutes.
From Sakuramachi Bus Terminal:
By Sanko-Bus: Take a bus for Ozu or Musashigaoka and get off at the "Ozekibashi bus stop."
By Kumaden bus: Take a bus for Tatsudaguchi/Kusunoki-danchi and get off at the "Ozekibashi bus stop."
By Taxi: Approximately 15 minutes.
From Kumamoto Airport:
By Sanko Bus: Get on the Limousine Bus headed for the Sakuramachi Bus Terminal and get off at the terminal. Take a Kumamoto-Shiei Bus for Tatsudaguchi/Kurokami-danchi or the Sanko-Bus for Ozu/Musashigaoka. Get off at the "Ozekibashi bus stop."
By Taxi: Approximately 40 minutes.
For more information such as rough costs for the above and one of recommended routes from

Application
Application Method
〈International House Residence Management System〉
Please apply through your academic supervisor who is eligible to download the "Application Format" from the International Residence Management System. International students before enrolling in Kumamoto University are not eligible to access to the System.
Your application will complete when the "Application Format" is registered on the International House Residence Management System.
International House Residence Management System (Accessing is available only on campus, and please use a browser other than Firefox)
URL：https://fgc.jimu.kumamoto-u.ac.jp/kokusai_kaikan/
International Students
Application period is twice a year; around January for spring semester and July for fall semester. Now we are accepting applications for the International House for academic year 2026 (fall semester). International students who request to reside in the International House are advised to carefully read Application Guideline, then submit the application through your academic supervisor by
July 17, 2026
.
*Please take note there would not be enough rooms for all applicants.
※Regarding an application beyond the application period, please contact Internation Student Office by email.
gji-ryugaku@jimu.kumamoto-u.ac.jp

International Researchers
Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis 2 months before moving-in. Please apply through your academic supervisor who is eligible to  download the "Application Fromat" from the Internation Residence Management System.
<NOTE> Such a international researchers whose contract with Kumamoto University is for more than one year is not eligible for the application of International House.

Rental Fees and Charges
Due to the recent increase in maintenance costs and other expenses caused by inflation, we plan to raise the room fees for C, D and E and common service fees by 8% to 10% starting from April 2027.
We will notify residents via the International House website or email as soon as the decision is made.
The increased room fees and common service fees are expected to be the amounts listed in the table below.
1. Payment of rent, property usage charges, electricity and water expenses
(1) Residents of Building A and B
International Students
The invoices for rent, expenses for common service, electricity and water charges are put into each mailbox around the 15th of every month. Residents must pay these charges at the Kokaibashi Branch of Higo Bank by the end of the month. Couple and family rooms are equipped with a gas range. Residents need to initiate a contract. For details on how to apply, use and pay for gas, follow the instructions provided by the gas company and the International House office.
Researchers
The invoices for property usage charges, expenses for common service, electricity and water charges are put into each mailbox around the 15th of every month. Residents must pay these charges at the Kokaibashi Branch of Higo Bank by the end of the month. Since the rooms for researchers are equipped with a gas range, residents need to initiate a contract. For details on how to apply for, use and pay for gas, follow the instructions provided by the gas company and the International House office.
(2) Residents of Building C and D
International Students
The invoices for rent, expenses for common service, electricity and water charges are put into each mailbox around the 15th of every month. Residents must pay these charges at the Kokaibashi Branch of Higo Bank by the end of the month.
(3) Residents of Building E
International Students
The invoices for rent and expenses for common service are put into each mailbox around the 15th of every month. Residents must pay these charges to the Kokaibashi Branch of Higo Bank by the end of the month. Since electricity and water must be contracted by the residents directly with the utility companies, follow the instructions of the International Student Office and the International House office for these.
Non-smoking in University Campuses
From July 1, 2019,
Kumamoto University is
100% smoke-free campus
. This includes International House (inside and outside of the buildings). Thank you for your understanding and cooperation to prevent exposure to secondhand smoke.

別紙 ２                                                                       
To International Student s, 
                                  Director of Institute for Education and Student Affairs  
 
Kumamoto University International House  
(Dorm itory  for Internati onal Students)  Appl ication  
             
This is to notify international students that the International House for academic year  2026 (Fall  Semester)  is now open for 
application.  
1. Application Method  
Please apply through your academic supervisor who is eligible to  download the "Application Format" from the 
International Residence Management System  which is accessible from the campus only . International students before 
enrolling in Kumamoto University are not eligible to access to the System.  Your applicatio n will complete when the 
"Application Format" is registered on the International House Residence Management System.   
 
 URL：https://fgc.jimu.kumamoto -u.ac.jp/kokusai_kaikan/  
                       ※ We have moved to a new system since 2025.  
 
2. Register Deadline : 
 July  17, 20 26 
* Registration for new application should be done through your academic supervisor, so please send the completed 
Application Form to your academic supervisor as soon a s possible.  You will receive a n email f rom the system once it ’s 
successfully  submitted . If you do not receive the email , please  check  with your academic supervisor . 
* Applicant s, who wish to reside  in the International House  but have  not received the examination result yet,  should apply  
before  the result . However,  their residence permits of those who fail the examination will be cancelled . 
* Exchange students under agreements between  universities or faculties have  priority over  the other students . Please take 
note t here would not be enough rooms for all applicants in the case of a lot of applications.  
 Also, we may not be able to meet your preferred room type . The selection results will be announced  between late July to 
early August .

4. Eligibility  (Applicants  must meet a ll of the following two  requirements ) 
  (1) New international students who will enroll in Kumamoto  Unive rsity  October 2026 .

  (2) International students who have not lived at the International House before (exclu sive  of elective course students).

after leaving Japan for a certain period are eligible to apply.

5. Period  of Residence

*Due to the large number of students  moving out at the end of February and August, you may be asked to move out up to 
around two weeks earlier than the  permitted residence . 
*The above move -out deadlines of February and August are set to prepare  for new international students en roll ing in April 
and October of the following year, respectively. Please check with the academic affairs office of your respective department 
for the move -in start date  of late September . 
* Regular students can stay at the International House for half a year  only . 
* Applicants, who wish to have a specific period of residence, are advised to consult with  the International Students Office 
individually.   
If no consultation takes place , the application will be treated as either  of the above -mentioned residency periods.  
* Depending on the student's affiliation and status , a different period of stay may be set.  
 6. Fees  (JPY per month )  
Due to the recent increase in maintenance costs and other expenses caused by inflation, we plan to raise  
the room fee s for C, D and E and common  service fee s by 8% to 10% starting from  April 2027.  
We will notify residents via the International  House  website or email as soon as the decision is made.  
The increased room fees and common service  fees are expected to be the amoun ts listed in the table below.  
 
 
（1）A deposit will be charged separately when moving in . The deposit will be refunded after taking out the cleaning 
fee and key replacement fee , if any equipment and furniture have no damage.   
（2）Monthly rent is pro-rated on  a daily basis  when moving in or out in the middle of the month, but the common 
service charge  is fixed that  will not  be prorated  excluding September when residents need to move in based 
on Kumamoto University ’s instruction.    
  （3）All residents must rent Futon (Bedding) during each permitted residency period.  
This fee is  non-refundable even if you move out  before the end of your  permitted residency period .  
For details,  please refer to  the International House website.

*  The opposite gender is forbidden  to enter  the shared room except for renter’s family members.  
* You must not lend out or duplicate International House keys.  
* There may be occasions when staff need to enter  rooms without notice in order to do emergency

Immigration and Pickup Service
Entry Procedures
Immigration inspection
Your passport and visa will be checked, and your status of residence and period of stay will be determined.
Baggage claim
After passing through immigration, pick up your baggage at the baggage claim area. If you cannot find your baggage, ask the staff there for assistance. Follow their instructions. Any late-arriving baggage will be sent to you as soon as possible. The flight charge for your baggage in this case will be covered by the airline.
Customs clearance
A customs officer will inspect your belongings. If you are carrying items such as alcoholic beverages or cigarettes, you may be required to pay a duty. Unaccompanied baggage that you had sent to Japan before your arrival must also be declared.
Pickup service (For Short-Term Exchange Students who are renting rooms at International House)
Kumamoto University staffs will pick you up at SAKURAMACHI Kumamoto Bus Terminal. The pickup service is available between 9:00 a.m. and about 4:00 p.m. on the designated date (except weekends and holidays).
Please complete a "Pickup Service Application Form" from a link sent by International Student Office before your departure. If you do not need the pickup service, please let us know your flight schedule.
If you require someone's help, please contact International Student Office (e-mail:
gji-ryugaku@jimu.kumamoto-u.ac.jp
Fax: +81-96-342-2103).

Passports and Visas
Passports and Visas
All international students applying to study in Japan must have a student visa that will remain valid for the duration of their studies. Before arrival in Japan, you must meet several requirements, as explained below.
Passport
It may take a long time for you to receive a passport after you apply for it. We recommend that you apply for your passport from your home country as early as possible.
Visa
Make sure that you obtain the appropriate visa. You will receive a visa with a student status because your purpose for coming to Japan is to study. If you arrive in Japan with a different type of visa, you will have to go through complicated procedures to change your visa status to the ""college student" designation. To avoid this problem, please be sure to obtain a "college student" visa before traveling to Japan.
a. Exchange students and privately funded students
As soon as you receive your Acceptance Letter and Certificate of Eligibility from Kumamoto University, please apply for a visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate in your home country. You will need to submit the certificates, your passport, and some photos. The length of the application process depends on the country issuing the visa. Students who are eligible for JASSO scholarships will receive a Certificate of Scholarship. Please also submit this, if necessary, when you apply for a visa.
b. Japanese government scholarship students (University recommendation)
A "Letter of Approval" will be issued and sent to you. You may then contact your nearest Japanese embassy/consulate to apply for your visa to enter Japan.

Air Tickets
Air Tickets
Air Tickets
a. Exchange students and privately funded students
Please purchase the tickets for your flight on your own, and ensure that you will arrive in Japan by the designated date.
b. Japanese government scholarship students
(1) Booking …
A: Embassy Recommendation
Japanese embassy or travel agency will book an air ticket for you.
B: University Recommendation
Kumamoto University will book an air ticket for you.
Complete the application form and send it immediately to the international Student Office of Kumamoto University by e-mail.
*Write your contact address in your home country using the Roman alphabet (kanji characters can be included).
(2) Receipt
For an e-ticket (electronic ticket), you will receive an electronic ticket receipt or an electronic ticket passenger itinerary receipt (name varies by airline) via e-mail.
The boarding ticket is issued at the airline check-in counter on the departure date.
Note:
* You cannot change your flight schedule or cash in the air ticket supplied to you.
* Since the air ticket must be submitted to MEXT after it has been used, you must submit the boarding ticket stub to Kumamoto University upon arrival.
* Please note that you must pay the transportation fee from the Japanese international airport at which you first arrive to Kumamoto.

Travel Information
Travel Information
Flight schedule
Pickup Service is available for Short-Term Exchange Students who are renting rooms at International House. Please complete a "Pickup Service Application Form"
from a link sent by International Student Office before your departure. If we cannot meet you as scheduled, you have to go to International House by yourself. If you are unable to depart as scheduled for some reasons, please contact us immediately (Tel: +81-96-342-2103 E-mail:
gji-ryugaku@jimu.kumamoto-u.ac.jp
).
Baggages
Generally, you are allowed to bring a maximum of 20 kg of baggage with you free of charge on the plane. If you exceed this limit, you will have to pay excess weight charges. You should bring only the most necessary items when you come to Japan. Once you settle in, you can buy most things you need in Japan, or you can have items sent to you from your home country. If you want to send unaccompanied baggage to Japan ahead of your arrival, please check with us first. Do not send it to the airport or university without consulting with us in advance.
Customs regulations
Your possessions, even those for personal use during your stay in Japan, will be inspected at customs and may be subject to customs duty. Please fully check the customs regulations before traveling to Japan.
In Japan, possession of any of the following is prohibited by law:
a. Stimulants, marijuana, and any other illegal drugs
b. Firearms and swords
c. Pornography (books/videotapes)
d. Articles that infringe upon such things as trademark rights and patent rights, e.g., counterfeit goods, etc.)
e. Wild animals and plants, or related goods that are regulated by the Washington Treaty.
(Do not violate this law, or you will be strictly punished and your scholarship will be revoked.)
If you bring animals and plants (including seeds and fruits) into Japan, you must go through quarantine. As there are many prohibited/restricted items, please carefully check the belongings you intend to bring into Japan; otherwise, your items may be confiscated.

Short-Term Exchange Program
Short-Term Exchange Program
"
Short-Term Exchange Program
(Brochure)"
Purpose
Kumamoto University Short-Term Exchange Program is designed for full-time foreign undergraduate students in their 2nd year or above from universities that have a student exchange agreement with Kumamoto University. The program offers courses on Japanese language, Japanese and Asian society and culture, advanced science and technology. At Kumamoto University, there are both half- and full-year programs, and students retain full-time student status at their home universities. This program encourages promotion of cultural and academic interactions between Kumamoto University and partner university students.
Available Courses and Qualifications
E Course (Program in English)
Students in this course mainly take Short-Term Exchange Program classes taught in English and some Japanese classes. Additionally, they have opportunities to attend non-credit Japanese language course for beginners during their stay.  Students who wish to take other classes must have a  consulatation with the office staff in advance. Also, those other classes will not be calculated towards program completion.
Eligibility
E Course
seeking applicants should be 2
nd
year students or above at the time of program start.
For non-native English speakers, submission of a copy of TOEFL score (iBT 61 or higher) is required (IELTS score is also accepted).
*Chinese CET, Indonesian ELPT are NOT adequate.
*A letter from a professor
CANNOT be accepted
as a proof of language proficiency.
Applicants should be physically and mentally capable of completing their studies for designated periods.
*Applicants should be able to hold the student VISA when she/he arrives in Japan.
J Course (Program in Japanese)
Students in this course mainly take classes in specialized subjects for undergraduate students of each faculty, as well as classes of the Japanese language. Also, they can take general education classes and Short-Term Exchange Program classes taught in English.
Eligibility
J Course
Applicants should be non-Japanese students.
Applicants for
J Course
should be 2
nd
year students or above at the time of program start.
Applicants should have Japanese ability equivalent to JLPT N2 level or better.
*A letter from a professor
CANNOT be accepted
as a proof of language proficiency.
Applicants should be physically and mentally capable of completing their studies for designated periods.
*Applicants should be able to hold the student VISA when she/he arrives in Japan.
Period of Acceptance
Students are accepted for a half year or one full year that starts in either October or April.
Application Package
Please contact the person in charge of outbound program at your university for application documents. Kumamoto University does not accept any mails sent by indivitual students.

Rules for living in the International House and Apartments
Rules for living in the International House and Apartments
Garbage disposal
・Observe designated times, days and places for putting out garbage.
・Put out your garbage on the morning of the designated day.
・Follow the garbage sorting rules.
Washing machines
・Be particularly careful about noise and water leaks. Avoid doing your laundry early in the morning or late at night.
・ Make sure the drainage hose does not get knocked out of the drainpipe. If you do not connect properly, it may cause water leakage and cause troubles in the rooms on the lower floors.
Fire Hazards
・Make sure you extinguish cigarettes.
・Do not smoke whtin the site.
・Be careful not to leave electrical appliances on (iron, heating appliances, etc.).
Miscellaneous
・Make sure you read and understand your rental contract and follow the conditions.
・Do not have guests to stay or sublet the apartment, even for short peiods, without the landlord's permission.
・Do not leave personal belongings on the communal corridors and passageways.
・Keep your apartment clean.
